articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz llega al tramo decisivo de las ATP Finals como el jugador más en forma del circuito. Ha ganado sus dos primeros partidos en Turín sin ceder un set, se ha clasificado para las semifinales como primero de grupo y suma once victorias consecutivas, desde que arrancó su camino al título en Viena ante Khachanov. El murciano se paga a cuota 1.61, una cifra que implica una probabilidad cercana al 62% y que refleja su superioridad en las últimas semanas. Su balance es extraordinario. Entre agosto y noviembre ha firmado un 22-2, tras un 22-3 entre enero y abril, y llega con tres títulos desde que regresó en el US Open, tras cinco meses de ausencia por una lesión de muñeca, entre ellos el Masters 1000 de París de la semana pasada. En Turín ha barrido a Frances Tiafoe y a Daniil Medvedev, al que ganó por 6-2 y 6-4 en apenas una hora y once minutos, con una profundidad y una precisión que el ruso admitió no poder contrarrestar. Además, ha logrado algo clave en el cuadro. Al quedar primero de su grupo, evita a Zverev hasta la final. Pero la gran incógnita es su estado físico. Alcaraz terminó el partido ante Medvedev con molestias en el isquiotibial izquierdo, con el muslo vendado, y se espera una resonancia magnética que determine su futuro en el torneo. Es un aviso importante en un jugador que ya ha convivido con lesiones durante todo el curso, y que condiciona el precio de su cuota en las casas de apuestas. Alexander Zverev es el segundo, a cuota 3.21. El alemán es el cabeza de serie número uno, tiene ya asegurado el número uno de final de año y se clasificó para las semifinales tras ganar a Jódar y a Shelton, con un balance de 6-0 en los duelos directos frente al estadounidense. Su cuota refleja que es el rival más serio de Alcaraz, aunque solo podría cruzarse con él en la final. Conoce bien la pista y la presión de este tipo de torneos, y la ausencia de un rival de su nivel en su mitad del cuadro es un argumento a favor. Daniil Medvedev se paga a 9.03. El ruso llegaba con tres derrotas consecutivas y solo una victoria en cuatro partidos en pista cubierta esta temporada, y su derrota ante Alcaraz no ha mejorado su situación. Es un jugador con experiencia en las rondas finales y con un tenis capaz de incomodar a cualquiera, pero su precio refleja que el mercado lo ve como una alternativa lejana. Ben Shelton cierra la lista, a cuota 12. El estadounidense venció a Alcaraz en las semifinales del US Open, un dato que alimenta su candidatura, y lucha por entrar entre los cuatro mejores de su grupo. articles.title: ‘A life changing blow’: Malaysian Commonwealth Games champion loses right arm after motorcycle crash
articles.summary: Malaysian weightlifter Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin has lost his right arm after a serious motorcycle crash in Kuala Lumpur.
articles.body: Malaysian weightlifter Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin has lost his right arm after a serious motorcycle crash in Kuala Lumpur. The 2026 Commonwealth Games gold medallist underwent an operation lasting about seven hours at Kuala Lumpur Hospital on November 17. Doctors amputated his arm above the elbow after efforts to save it failed. Three days after the accident, Hafizuddin was currently awake and in a stable condition, according to Malaysian Weightlifting Federation president Ayub Rahmat. The news has shocked Malaysia’s sporting community, but officials say they will support him through treatment and help him plan his future.Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin Loses Right Arm After Seven-Hour Surgery Following Motorcycle AccidentHafizuddin was riding along the Sungai Besi-Ulu Kelang Elevated Expressway, known as the SUKE Highway, at around 11pm on November 16. He was travelling from Ampang towards Bukit Jalil when he reportedly lost control of his motorcycle.The National Sports Council said he suffered injuries to his legs, shoulder and head. Doctors also found a collection of blood near his right shoulder. He was taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital, where he received urgent medical care.The most serious damage was to his right arm. It had broken bones and severe injuries to the blood vessels. Doctors first tried to save the limb during the long operation. However, they later decided that removing it above the elbow was necessary to protect his life.Malaysian Weightlifting Federation president Ayub Rahmat confirmed the operation and later gave an update on Hafizuddin’s condition. Speaking to AFP on November 19, Ayub said: "He is awake and smiling." He added that the athlete’s physical condition was improving, although the accident had changed his future.The Malaysian government has said it will cover the cost of Hafizuddin’s treatment and medical care. The support will also include follow-up care and hospital accommodation until he is discharged. His training allowance is set to continue at its current rate, according to Youth and Sports Minister Taufiq Johari.The National Sports Council is also expected to help with his recovery. Officials have said that support for the athlete and his family remains a priority.Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin's 2026 Commonwealth Games Gold Medal and Future in WeightliftingThe crash came only a few months after Hafizuddin reached the biggest milestone of his career. He won the men’s 88kg weightlifting gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, in July.He lifted a total of 345kg to take the title. His result included a 162kg snatch and a 183kg clean and jerk. The snatch also set a Malaysian national record and a Commonwealth Games record.That win made Hafizuddin one of Malaysia’s leading young weightlifters and put him on the radar ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. His loss of an arm means he is no longer expected to continue as a competitive weightlifter.However, the Malaysian Weightlifting Federation is looking at ways to keep him connected to the sport. Ayub said the federation was considering a future role for him in coaching, potentially at state level in Perlis, where Hafizuddin is from.The federation has also spoken about providing support as he adjusts to life after the accident. The focus now is on his medical care and recovery, while officials work out what kind of role may be possible for him later.Hafizuddin’s case has also drawn support from Malaysia’s sports leadership. Youth and Sports Minister Taufiq Johari visited him in hospital, while national sports bodies have promised help for his treatment and longer-term needs. His family has asked for privacy as he recovers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua shares extreme daily diet and water intake as Tyson Fury fight gets closer
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua is taking his preparation seriously ahead of his December 11 showdown with Tyson Fury in Cardiff.
articles.body: Anthony Joshua is taking his preparation seriously ahead of his December 11 showdown with Tyson Fury in Cardiff. The former heavyweight champion has revealed that his training camp involves eating between 4,000 and 4,500 calories every day and drinking around 10 litres of water. While his food intake is already far above what most people need, Joshua says staying hydrated is an even bigger part of his daily routine. The 37-year-old also opened up about his possible retirement and what he wants to do after leaving boxing.Anthony Joshua Explains His 4,500-Calorie Diet and 10-Litre Water Routine Ahead of Tyson Fury FightThe long-awaited meeting between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury is finally getting closer. The British rivals will meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11, ending years of talk about a fight that boxing fans have wanted to see.With the date approaching, Joshua is putting extra attention into his body and training. The 6ft 6in heavyweight recently spoke to The Sun's Clemmie Moodie about the amount of food and water he needs during fight camp.Joshua revealed that he eats between 4,000 and 4,500 calories every day while preparing for a fight. That is a huge amount of food, but his training demands a lot of energy. As a heavyweight boxer, he needs to maintain his strength while keeping up with long and demanding training sessions.However, food is not the only thing he watches closely. Joshua explained that drinking enough water takes even more attention during his preparation."People talk about how many calories they eat. The thing is, is how many litres of water we have to drink. I think I go for about 10 litres of water a day," he told The Sun.His daily water intake caught Moodie's attention during the conversation. She asked whether drinking so much water meant he had to visit the bathroom throughout the day and wake up during the night.Joshua admitted that managing the amount of water he drinks is not always simple. He also explained how he handles it before going to sleep."You have to stagger the way you drink the water before bed, like 500 millilitres, a litre here, then another 500," he said.His routine is built around the needs of his training camp. However, his water intake should not be treated as a target for everyone, as hydration needs can vary from person to person.Anthony Joshua Opens Up About Retirement and His Plans After BoxingWhile the Tyson Fury fight remains his main focus, Joshua also spoke about life after boxing. The former two-time unified heavyweight champion admitted that he is starting to think more seriously about retirement.He explained that his approach to the sport has always been about discipline rather than enjoying every part of the lifestyle that comes with being a famous boxer."That's the motto I have with boxing. Boxing is not glamorous," Joshua said."I keep it pretty simple, straightforward. I do what I can. I live by what I need, not by what I want. And it's working out."Joshua also shared an idea about what he might do once his boxing career comes to an end. He mentioned investing in Under Armour and possibly becoming a shareholder in the sportswear company."And then I think when I finish fighting, I'll be more chilled and then maybe I can go and look at investing in Under Armour stocks or maybe have a share in the Under Armour company or something like that. But as for now, I'm pretty content," he added.The British boxer also spoke about his age and admitted that retirement may not be too far away."I can't believe I'm 37. It's crazy. So when am I going to retire? I think, yes, pretty soon. I'm getting old now," he said.He later added: "From an athlete's point of view, I'm getting old."Joshua made it clear that he does not believe he has many years left in the sport."So maybe that will be our next sit down when we talk about plans for after boxing, because that will be coming around pretty soon. I haven't got many years ahead of me," he said.For now, his attention remains on December 11. The fight against Tyson Fury could become one of the biggest nights of Joshua's career, while his comments suggest he is also thinking about what comes next.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fantasy Football: From chasing history to breakouts, 1 thing to watch in all 32 WR rooms for the second half
articles.summary: Matt Harmon breaks down what he’s watching in every NFL team’s WR room for the second half of the fantasy season.
articles.body:
With the second half of the season in full swing, here's what Yahoo analyst Matt Harmon is looking for in each team's WR room for fantasy football.

Zay Flowers tries to keep a high-end season afloat

After a blistering start to the year, Flowers is now WR8 in yards per route run and WR16 in points per game. It was tracking to be so much better than this before quarterback chaos sunk the Ravens' passing game. In Jacoby Brissett's first start, the Ravens dropped back over 50 times, a rarity in the Lamar Jackson era , but the passing tree wasn't consolidated whatsoever. Flowers was targeted on 14.9% of his routes, the lowest rate of the season. Both fantasy managers and a Ravens team that desperately needs to win require the ball in Flowers' hands much more often than that, even if he ultimately fumbled the game away in Week 10.

When DJ Moore has been available for the Bills, all the mainstay passing-game players get a bump. On plays where Moore is on the field, Khalil Shakir averages 2.03 yards per route and Dalton Kincaid averages 3.15. Kincaid specifically drops to 1.97 when Moore isn't on the field. This is because Moore, who averages a whopping 16.6 air yards per target, has been a huge add as a coverage-dictator and vertical threat. Moore isn't going to be a WR1-level producer but he's key to the health of this offense and is capable of spike weeks in this ecosystem.

Right now, the Bengals have the WR4 and WR6 in points per game on their roster. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been masterful this season with Joe Burrow playing the best football of his career. Each receiver has five games inside the top-10 of weekly fantasy scoring. The Bengals offense has used condensed formations, and the leap in their offensive line's pass-blocking has been a key factor. Quietly, Dohnte Meyers is emerging as a credible option as the WR3 who can play multiple positions, which has also allowed them to be more creative with the deployment. I see no reason this train slows down any time soon.

Do we see Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion's roles blend at all?

So far this season, Denzel Boston has been used as a downfield X-receiver and KC Concepcion has been a movement option who runs over 60% of his routes from the slot. I'm not critiquing that deployment, as both are excellent options in those roles and have been fantastic to start their rookie seasons. However, I believe Boston is capable of being weaponized with some reps as a big slot and Concepcion can win outside against man coverage. If those roles start to blend down the stretch, or especially in future seasons, these guys can be even more productive.

Any hope for a second-half ascension for Jaylen Waddle and Co.?

Call it hope or call it cope, but we can blame my favorite strength-of-schedule zealot, Justin Boone, for even getting me to keep the light on. Coming out of the bye, the Broncos have games against the Raiders (twice), Steelers, Jets, Dolphins, Bills and Patriots. Only the Steelers look like a potential trouble spot for passing games. I hesitate to say it can't get worse but it would be tough to imagine. Waddle has finished inside the top-24 weekly scoring receivers just twice, which is only one fewer game than every other Denver wide receiver combined (Pat Bryant twice, Courtland Sutton once). I'm hoping the offense has a clearer vision for how to maximize the player they traded major draft picks for, as well as a more confident player under center.

Rotation participation numbers for Tank Dell

In his last two games coming back from the team's Week 8 bye, Tank Dell has run a route on 55% and 54.8% of the dropbacks. The team has used guys like Xavier Hutchinson ahead of him and had him in a rotation with Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kayshon Boutte. There's a good chance this usage holds for Dell as he continues to work his way back from a serious injury. I'm still comfortable betting on him as an upside WR3 because he looks great on tape and is being used on downfield breaking routes. You just have to know you're dealing with a volatile projection with that playing time.

Not much here but does Deion Burks flash anything?

The Colts traded their best 2026 receiver at the deadline in Josh Downs and sent away a steady veteran in Keenan Allen. Their highly paid X-receiver, Alec Pierce, is on IR and I'm not expecting him to be back this year. Laquon Treadwell will lead this group in routes run as the every-down X-receiver going forward in a passing game that's been among the worst in the NFL, thanks to quarterback play. We don't need to fret the Colts' room much at this stage but I'm at least curious if any young players can flash to earn a role in 2027. Deion Burks is an interesting rookie with some juice who has gotten reps all year as a downfield Z-receiver.

Jacksonville dominating the intermediate area

The Jaguars are one of the toughest teams to prepare for in the NFL right now. This offense can run so many concepts out of multiple personnel groupings and has a litany of viable role players. Meanwhile, Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington are two of the league's most productive receivers on throws of 10-20 air yards. In competitive games and good matchups, these two should roll, especially Washington.

Playing time for the new-look wide receiver room

Josh Downs' arrival in Kansas City paid immediate dividends for the offense. He was targeted five times on eight routes. Those numbers are only going up. The question is how high he can go and who comes off the field more often. Xavier Worthy seems like the natural answer given his play through three seasons, but his speed also brings tactical value by lifting coverages. Rashee Rice and Downs should be more complementary as they go. Additionally, Cyrus Allen's emergence as a talented route-runner and deep-ball option makes this even more complicated. I think Downs emerges as an every-week fantasy starter but we have playing time questions to answer to understand the ceiling.

Does anyone show they deserve a 2027 role?

Tre Tucker has been the team's best receiver but will be a free agent. He's a good player but mostly a vertical-only receiver. Meanwhile, Jalen Nailor has looked overstretched as an every-down starter. Second-year receiver Jack Bech is a nice role player but hasn't emerged as a highly-targeted option and missed a chunk of time with an injury. The Raiders will use the rest of the season to simply assess if any of these guys will be in the rotation in 2027, or if they will need to start fresh.

I've been ready to see more of Tre' Harris and less of Quentin Johnston since the first month of the season. Johnston has never fully developed and, frankly, looks like he's regressed in 2026. Meanwhile, Harris continues to flash a nice ability to separate and play multiple positions. He's run a route on more than 90% of the dropbacks just twice this year and compiled 60 yards on three catches in Week 4 and 86 on five last week. I'd love to watch Ladd McConkey take off in the back half, but I just worry he's not physically up for the task. He averages 2.25 yards per route run this year, so he's been good, but he just can't stay on the field.

Caleb Douglas leads all rookies with 2.27 yards per route run and the tape has been rock-solid. He is clearly a hit for the Dolphins. Now, let's find out how good he is. Malik Willis' injury will likely complicate things from a production standpoint. Yet, Douglas registered a season-high 155 air yards and caught three passes for 71 yards last week with Kyle McCord under center. Douglas has hit at least 70 yards in three of his last four games.

When the Patriots return from their bye week, they will do so without Drake Maye under center. The season is slowly slipping away for this team as they are buried under a mountain of injuries. It's just not going to be their year. The rest of the season should be dedicated to figuring out which members of the wide receiver room should have big roles in 2027 and beyond. That includes A.J. Brown, who has been unable to stay healthy and doesn't look right when he's been available. I'm not sure he'll be on the roster next year, which leaves Romeo Doubs and a collection of WR3 and WR4 types. This room needs an upgrade.

Despite playing in very different roles, we haven't seen many games where AD Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. both go off at the same time. That's especially tough when Garrett Wilson is available. The Jets have a strong trio of receivers with these guys on the roster and my sense is that they'll all be on the team in 2027. The rest of the way, we need to look at their individual matchups and success to try and pinpoint the right weeks Mitchell and Cooper can get going. This will also help us assess what the pecking order looks like behind Wilson next season in what, hopefully, is an improved overall ecosystem.

Does Germie Bernard lose snaps to Roman Wilson and/or Michael Pittman Jr.?

Germie Bernard looked like he might be one of those second-half-of-the-season rookie breakouts about a month ago. Yet, he's failed to clear 30 yards in any of his last three games. While I think he's a good player, you wonder if he has missed his window to cement a starting job. The Steelers will likely get veteran Michael Pittman Jr. back soon, along with Roman Wilson. The Bernard and Wilson playing time splits will be quite interesting since Wilson gave this team a real man coverage answer early in the year.

How does Carnell Tate blend back into a slightly changed offense?

The Titans have found an answer to boosting Cam Ward in recent weeks: Tennessee has used no huddle on 45% of their snaps in each game on either side of the bye week. No other team is even above 18%. Ward operates well with tempo and from spread concepts. No surprise, this has resulted in Ward's two best games of the season. That's without Carnell Tate in the mix, who has been excellent on tape this year and a real weapon down the field. Once he's healthy, Tate's ability to quickly separate on routes over the middle in this new-look attack should result in some big weeks.

I'll be frank, this might be the bleakest wide receiver room I can remember in recent memory after they lost Michael Wilson for the season and placed Kendrick Bourne on IR. The only guy who is moderately interesting is Day 3 rookie, Reggie Virgil. He's a slower, poor man's Robbie Anderson from his days with the Panthers. Someone has to run routes for this team; catches may be optional.

Can Jahan Dotson continue to be a big-play threat?

We know what Drake London can do but not enough people are giving Jahan Dotson praise for the rebound season he is having. Dotson leads all wide receivers with 30-plus targets with 21.9 yards per catch. He's been a real nice answer for the team as a deep option down the field. His ability here has allowed the Falcons to keep London in a movement Z and slot-heavy role.

Who emerges as the layup option between Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan?

The Panthers need to change up their approach on offense. What worked to smash teams early in the season has become unworkable as pass-protection issues have cropped up. Bryce Young leads the NFL in pass attempts with pressure arriving in 2.5 seconds or faster. On those throws, Tetairoa McMillan averages almost 17 air yards per target and Jalen Coker is at almost 10. These receivers run long, developing routes to hit chunk plays and that's a thin line to walk when you can't hold up in protection.

Do Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III stay in isolated roles?

This season, Rome Odunze averages 14.9 air yards per target, which leads the team by a wide margin and Luther Burden is at 7.4. The Bears aren't doing anything wrong here and both are thriving in their respective roles; there's just no overlap between the two. I believe Odunze can win in the short area as a chain-mover more often and Burden can get open in the intermediate area. Blending those would allow Odunze to be targeted more often and keep Burden involved for all four quarters.

Is this George Pickens' swan song with Dallas?

At this rate, I'd be shocked if George Pickens returns to Dallas after an up-and-down season with the team on the franchise tag, especially with CeeDee Lamb turning in a dominant performance. Pickens will likely be motivated to put up more big performances after his Week 10 outing, which was the second-highest scoring game for a receiver all season. Keep an eye on his likely replacement, Ryan Flournoy, who has scored as a top-24 receiver in five of his last six games. He's already a viable option.

Is it Jameson Williams over Sam LaPorta in the target tree now?

Over the last five weeks, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams account for 51% of the team's targets. Sam LaPorta is a relatively distant third at 14%. For much of the last two years, it's really been a push and pull between LaPorta and Williams for the second target option — rarely have they popped off together. The Lions have jumped their use of heavy personnel considerably in this post-bye span, which has contributed to the wideouts getting more burn, especially Williams, who runs a route on a team-high 90% of the dropbacks since Week 6. This is how we get more consistent weekly production from the volatile wideout.

Matthew Golden has been one of the breakout stars at the wide receiver position this year. He's the WR8 in points per game behind his teammate Christian Watson. That's been despite leading the league in drops by a considerable margin. Fantasy Points Data has charged Golden with 13 drops this year, almost double the amount of the second-highest receiver in AD Mitchell with eight. He's also won just three of his 11 contested targets. I'm always the first guy to suggest you just live with drop issues and continue to build the wideout's confidence so they can push past them. The Packers and Jordan Love appear to be taking that approach. If he can ever clean these issues up, the ceiling is quite high for Golden and he's already been excellent; scary proposition.

The Rams used a ton of 20 personnel in Week 10, with both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams on the field along with three wide receivers. For the most part, that was a collection of small speed-based options to hit big plays while the backs operate as checkdown outlets. It was a good bit of problem-solving by Sean McVay as injuries hit the receiver room but it's likely not sustainable. Now, if we can add Davante Adams to the mix as an intermediate answer to balance the scales, it could become a feature personnel grouping. The veteran could return in Week 12 or 13.

I'm not asking for much here. Justin Jefferson should continue to be the featured player. He registered 13 targets in Week 10. He had not seen 13-plus looks in a game since the Sam Darnold 2024 season. We just need complementary pieces to add pop to the other touches and layer in new dimensions to the offense with Kirk Cousins under center. I'll admit to enjoying the work of Myles Price and Tai Felton in place of some of the other guys who were previously putting the Vikings into schematic binds. Both averaged 6.0 yards or more after the catch per reception. Cousins having someone to spit the ball out to in the short area and get additional yards helps keep the offense on schedule.

Since Jordyn Tyson has been activated, he's taken over half his snaps from the slot and lined up off the ball on 80% of them. No wide receiver has been used in motion more than Tyson the last two weeks. He's been able to gobble up easy receptions while being targeted on 38% of his routes. That's awesome for his usage in fantasy but it was not a great plan for the Saints' offense, particularly in Week 10, when they ranked 23rd out of 28 teams in my offensive efficiency score. Tyson can get open in the intermediate area and Chris Olave shouldn't be left to run vertical stretch routes only. Tyson is an awesome player in this slot movement role but we can't overindex on the short passes, especially since he's not a run-after-catch threat.

Malik Nabers status as he pushes for tier 1

Malik Nabers was looking close to 100% healthy prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye and enjoyed some strong moments with J.J. McCarthy against the Texans. The two games since have been less enjoyable. While it's easy to blame McCarthy for the issues and he's far from blameless, Nabers has left some plays on the field as well. I hold Nabers in extremely high regard and believe he is the next guy who could graduate to Tier 1 (Ja'Marr Chase, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, etc. grouping) at the receiver position. I'd love to see him knock down that door in the back-half of the season. He needs to rebound from two of his less inspiring outings in back-to-back weeks.

In Weeks 7 to 9, Makai Lemon owned a near 27% share of the Eagles targets. Despite four out-of-character drops, Lemon still averaged 61.7 yards per game and snagged 19 receptions. He was starting to look like the layup slot funnel you'd hope for from his archetype of receiver. However, the target competition is about to ramp up with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks due back from injuries soon. How the Lemon and Smith, in particular, target distribution goes will inform us on how the situation may play out next season, as the Eagles play out the string for the rest of 2026.

The 49ers have the oldest wide receiver room I can remember with five guys over 31 years old taking snaps for the team in 2026. Yet, they keep rolling. Deebo Samuel Sr. has settled into a pure gadget role and barely operates as a true receiver. Keenan Allen arrived in the middle of last week and immediately earned a first down on 19.1% of his routes. He's going to be quite helpful down the stretch. When Mike Evans is healthy, he's still a fantastic starting X-receiver.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 1,207 yards on 79 catches (109 targets) through 10 weeks of the NFL season. You'd do backflips if your favorite sleeper receiver did that over a full season. Smith-Njigba is on pace to clear 2,000 yards this season. He'd be the first wideout in NFL history to do it. Based on his own individual play despite teams crafting coverages to stop him, and the lack of a true secondary threat, there's no reason to expect him to slow down anytime soon.

I'm very confident that Emeka Egbuka is a good NFL player but the Buccaneers need him to be great. We've yet to see that version of the player this season. To be fair, Egbuka has been dogged by injuries since training camp and the guy we saw against the Bears prior to the bye week was the worst version I've watched on tape in 2026. Hopefully a week off helps him get back to form as he heads into a good matchup against the Lions defense. Egbuka's 20.8% slot rate in Week 9 was the lowest of the season; that needs to rise in future weeks.

Antonio Williams turning chances into production

Since the team returned from the bye, Antonio Williams has led the team in routes run. He looks good on tape and gets easy separation in the intermediate area. However, he hasn't been consistently involved in the offense (16% target share). The Commanders spread the ball around, and he's competing with an excellent receiver in Stefon Diggs, who leads the team over the last three weeks with a 25% target-per-route rate. Williams can still make some big plays but we need him to get the ball more consistently to be an every-week option in fantasy. He does remain and excellent buy in dynasty leagues.

articles.title: Forfeitures could be a lesson for Total Chess organisers
articles.summary: BUDAPEST: Magnus Carlsen repeated his Houdini act on Wednesday, going missing from the table for the Fast Classic game against Bibisara Assaubayeva in the
articles.body: BUDAPEST: Magnus Carlsen repeated his Houdini act on Wednesday, going missing from the table for the Fast Classic game against Bibisara Assaubayeva in the ongoing Total Chess Pilot event here, after ensuring that he could not lose. This time, he was not alone. Abhimanyu Mishra and Richard Rapport followed the leader into forfeiting their Fast Classic games, the former against R Vaishali.The Indian Grandmaster was left ruing a missed opportunity for some game practice ahead of her Women's World Championship match against Ju Wenjun. Mishra now runs into Vaishali's brother R Praggnanandhaa in a contest for the 21st place. Rapport could not have beaten Haik Martirosyan even if he had won the Fast Classic.Anish Giri and Alireza Firouzja will compete for the crown over the next two days. Although Giri comfortably sailed past Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, Firouzja needed the Armageddon to beat Fabiano Caruana.The story of the knockouts, however, has been the forfeitures.In this event where all the three formats of the game are coming into play to zero in on the 'complete chess champion', a maximum of 20 points is up for grabs across four games of Blitz, two of Rapid and one of Fast Classic.The Fast Classic, which gives the winner 8 points, happens last. So, if a player gains at least 10.5 from Blitz (1 point for a win and .5 for draw) and Rapid (4 points for the winner and 2 for a draw), he might well consider it futile to play the Fast Classic. Although the question of ethics might come up, a player cannot be faulted for the forfeiture.In a World Championship match of 14 games, with one point for a win and .5 for a draw, the contest ends as soon as a player reaches 7.5 points.Organisers of Total Chess could well take this leaf out of the World Championship book. articles.summary: One of the most exciting majors of the year is almost here!
articles.body:
The revamped Grand Slam of Darts begins this month, with 48 players competing for one of the sport's most coveted titles.

The event has some key changes, so it's important to know the details before watching the action unfold.

What to know about the Grand Slam of Darts

Let's take a look at some of the specifics of the tournament.

2026 Grand Slam of Darts Draw/group stage

Here are 16 different groups for the group stage.

*The table leader after the round-robin stage is completed will advance to the last 16

Nathan Aspinall vs. Maik Kuivenhoven (P)

*Matches played between Saturday afternoon's losing players and players from the group who haven't played yet

Luke Woodhouse vs. Krzysztof Ratajski (J)

*Matches played between Saturday evening's losing players and players from the group who haven't played yet

*Matches played between Saturday's winning player and the player who played their first match of the event on Sunday (Groups A-H)

*Matches played between Saturday's winning player and the player who played their first match of the event on Sunday (Groups I-P)

Gabriel Clemens vs. Rusty-Jake Rodriguez (O)

Michael van Gerwen vs. Jeffrey de Graaf (L)

Here is the bracket for the event after the group stage.

The Grand Slam of Darts is a 48-player tournament (16 more players than 2025), with various qualification routes to get there.

The seeded players consist of the top-16 players, who are each assigned to a separate group, and then have two additional players assigned to their group in the event's draw (one player from pool #2 and #3, with #2 having higher-ranked qualifiers than #3).

The first four days of the tournament (Nov. 14 - 17) will be purely group stage games, as each player will play the other two players in their group (round-robin format). These games will be played to best-of-9 legs.

The winner of each group will advance to the last 16. If there were to be a three-player tie, it would be determined by leg difference and then legs won, legs won against throw, tournament average and lastly a nine-dart shootout.

The knockout stage (last 16) will begin on Nov. 18. The first round of the knockout stage is played to best-of-19 legs.

The final three rounds (quarterfinals, semifinals & final) of the tournament will take place from Nov. 18 - 22 and will all be played to best-of-31 legs.

articles.title: Vermont ousts North Florida from NCAA Tournament with 2-1 overtime win
articles.summary: The University of North Florida played Vermont on Nov. 19 in the NCAA men’s soccer tournament. Did the Ospreys survive in New England?
articles.body:
It can't get much more agonizing for the University of North Florida men's soccer team .

For the third season in a row, the Ospreys were knocked out of the NCAA Tournament in the first round by either a one-goal margin or in penalty kicks. Vermont's Jack McDowell took a crossing pass from Luis Vetter with 4:14 left in overtime and jammed the ball past UNF keeper Luciano Natolia for a sudden-death goal that gave the Catamounts a 2-1 victory on Nov. 19 at Virtue Field in Burlington, Vt.

UNF (13-5-3) fell behind 1-0 in the 34th minute on Luis Fischer's goal but tied it with 41 seconds left in the half when Ponte Vedra High graduate and senior forward Mark Romano scored off assists by senior forward Alex Monde and senior midfielder Anton Khelil .

The breakaway goal from the right side was Romano's ninth goal of the season to tie Aron Martinez of Florida Gulf Coast for the most in the ASUN and Khelil's sixth assist, moving him into a tie for third in the conference.

The two teams battled through the final 45 minutes before going to overtime. Natoli and the Ospreys held off a late barrage of Vermont shots and Cats goalkeeper Niklas Herceg saved a direct kick from 30 yards out by Khelil.

Stepan Fiker of Vermont started the game-winning play with a pass to Vetter, who crossed the ball from the left side to McDowell.

Vermont (11-2-5), an at-large team from the America East Conference, advances to a second-round game on Nov. 22 at Clemson. UNF, which won its third consecutive ASUN title for an automatic berth in the NCAA by beating Queens on Nov. 14 2-0, is still looking for its first-ever NCAA Tournament victory.

The Ospreys lost to North Carolina last year in penalty kicks, 6-5, after regulation and two overtimes ended in a 2-2 tie. UNF fell to West Virginia 2-1 in 2024 and lost to Coastal Carolina 1-0 in 2015.

articles.title: Lakers Linked to 3 Centers After Jazz Exposes Costly Weakness
articles.summary: The Lakers' loss to a depleted Jazz team exposed a troubling weakness, and three potential trade options could offer help. The post Lakers Linked to 3 Center...
articles.body:
The Lakers' nine-game winning streak ended with more than a disappointing loss. It exposed a frontcourt problem that could become increasingly difficult to ignore.

Los Angeles fell 109-97 to the Utah Jazz on Wednesday, surrendering the rebounding battle to a team missing three of its most prominent big men.

Utah played without Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkić. Yet the Jazz outrebounded the Lakers 45-42, with Mo Bamba collecting 16 rebounds.

The defeat reinforced concerns raised by Michael Duarte of the California Post, who recently identified three potential backup center options for Los Angeles: Milwaukee's Jericho Sims, former Laker Jaxson Hayes and Clippers veteran Brook Lopez.

For a Lakers team with championship ambitions, finding reliable help behind Walker Kessler could become a priority.

Lakers Outrebounded by Short-Handed Jazz

Kessler returned Wednesday after missing the Lakers' overtime victory against Charlotte because of right lower leg soreness.

He finished with 10 points and 11 rebounds, but struggled offensively, shooting 3-for-7 from the field and 4-for-10 from the free-throw line.

His backup, Sandro Mamukelashvili, endured an even tougher night.

Mamukelashvili managed six points and three rebounds in nearly 21 minutes. He missed nine of his 10 field-goal attempts, including all four shots from beyond the arc.

Kevon Looney, who started against Charlotte during Kessler's absence, did not play Wednesday because of a coach's decision.

The Lakers received little help elsewhere.

Jarred Vanderbilt grabbed five rebounds but went scoreless, while the team's offense sputtered throughout the second half.

Luka Dončić scored 29 points but shot 10-for-28 and committed nine turnovers.

Los Angeles made just nine of 33 three-point attempts and shot 38.2% overall.

Utah outscored the Lakers 31-21 in the fourth quarter, snapping their winning streak.

Brook Lopez Among Lakers' Potential Center Options

Duarte identified Lopez as an intriguing possibility because of his combination of rim protection and outside shooting.

The veteran Clippers center could give coach JJ Redick a different option when Kessler rests while providing additional spacing for Dončić.

Sims offers a more traditional interior presence.

The Milwaukee center could provide rebounding, athleticism and energy around the basket, although his limited offensive range would do little to address Los Angeles' perimeter shooting.

Hayes represents a familiar alternative.

The former Lakers center, now with Utah, finished Wednesday's game with six points, seven rebounds and two blocks against his former team.

His athleticism and familiarity with Redick's system could make a reunion worth considering.

However, Duarte's suggestions are potential fits, not confirmation that trade negotiations are underway.

Rob Pelinka Faces Important Roster Decision

The Lakers' frontcourt depth was already tested Tuesday when Kessler sat out against Charlotte.

Los Angeles survived that game behind Quentin Grimes' 47-point performance.

Wednesday's defeat showed that getting Kessler back does not automatically solve the problem.

Even against a depleted Utah frontcourt, the Lakers struggled to control the glass and received minimal offensive support from their reserve big men.

A backup center alone would not fix their shooting or turnover issues.

But for president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka, strengthening the position could provide valuable insurance as the season progresses.

The Lakers have demonstrated their potential during an impressive start.

Their loss to Utah offered a reminder that their roster still has weaknesses worth addressing.

articles.title: Bleacher Report Power Rankings: Browns land at the 14 spot

articles.body:
Last week it felt like the Cleveland Browns season was circling the drain. They had lost two games in a row and fallen out of the playoff picture. It felt inevitable that the slide would continue as they took on a very talented Houston Texans team.

Once again, the Browns defense made life difficult on its opponent and provided an opportunity for the Deshaun Watson-led offense to chip away at the deficit before making big plays down the stretch."

He described the Browns as resilient in his evaluation, and it's hard to argue that. Anytime it has felt like their backs have been against the wall, this team has responded. Now they need to show that they can still keep this mindset up as a team that is becoming expected to make the postseason.

Welcome to GPblog's live coverage of the second free practice session for the 2026 Formula 1 Las Vegas GP. After an extraordinary opening session in which not a single driver managed to set a lap time, the teams will be hoping for considerably more running under the lights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Las Vegas GP weekend begins with unprecedented FP1 washout

The opening practice session in Las Vegas produced one of the most unusual scenes in recent Formula 1 history, as heavy rain prevented every driver from recording a single representative lap time.

Despite the session running its full scheduled duration, the timing screens remained empty, with Sergio Perez technically appearing at the top of the classification after venturing onto the circuit without completing a timed lap.

The extraordinary conditions left teams without any meaningful data from the opening hour, making FP2 particularly important as preparations continue for qualifying and Saturday night's Grand Prix.

With the Las Vegas Circuit featuring long straights, heavy braking zones and relatively low levels of downforce, drivers will be eager to understand how their cars perform around the challenging street layout. Tyre temperatures could also prove crucial, particularly given the cooler conditions traditionally experienced during nighttime running in Las Vegas.

Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull prepare for crucial FP2 session

Mercedes enter the weekend with plenty of attention surrounding their performance, having introduced four aerodynamic updates specifically designed to improve efficiency around the Las Vegas circuit.

Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull have also brought modifications as teams look to maximise their competitiveness on one of the fastest street circuits on the calendar.

The championship battle adds another layer of intrigue to the weekend, with Max Verstappen, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton all looking to strengthen their positions in the drivers' standings.

With no meaningful running completed in FP1, the second practice session now represents the first real opportunity for teams to evaluate their setups, gather tyre data and assess their long-run pace.

Will the weather finally allow the drivers to get some proper running under their belts, or could Las Vegas deliver another extraordinary session? Follow our liveblog below for all the latest updates from FP2.

articles.title: Dodgers Face Race Against Clock to Sign Japanese Phenom Shoki Oda
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers and teenage sensation Shoki Oda are facing a tight, complicated timeline to close a deal before the MLB lockout.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and teenage sensation Shoki Oda are facing a tight, complicated timeline to close a deal before the MLB lockout.

The Dodgers are in the race for Oda , who has met with 10 teams as nearly half the league is interested in him.

LA is the prohibitive favorite for Oda, but even if they secure a commitment, the timeline will be tricky.

How the lockout may impact the Shoki Oda pursuit

If the league wasn't facing a prolonged pause in action, the Dodgers' pursuit of Oda might be straightforward: wait until Jan 15, 2027, and offer him a massive amateur international free-agent bonus.

The current international amateur free agency window ends on Dec. 15, and the lockout starts on Dec. 1, leaving Oda and the Dodgers less than two weeks if LA can muster up a solid offer with their remaining bonus money.

If the Dodgers are out of bonus pool funds or low on them, Oda and the Dodgers may be waiting for either the money to kick in January or the new collective bargaining agreement to establish new rules for signing international amateurs.

During the last lockout, teams got their bonus pool money refreshed, which would be the best case for Oda.

However, international free agency could be overhauled.

According to Chunichi Sports, a Japanese news outlet , "Oda understands that he will not be able to sign a contract during the lockout period," the story read after translation.

For a player like Oda, if he wants to join a big-league team and avoid the Japanese NPB posting rules, he can either apply for amateur free agency or sign with a college and enter the amateur draft in a handful of years.

With modern NIL rules, Oda has a path to make a good deal of money in college, but he would be forced to stay for three years.

College seems unlikely, while a return to Japan, to the Yomiuri Giants where he was drafted, is still a long shot.

Given how definitive the signals are about his commitment to playing in America, he will need a major mindset shift.

For the Dodgers, the best they can hope for is a handshake agreement from Oda to sign for as much bonus money as reasonably possible, whether in January or down the line.

Anything short of that, and the rest of the teams lurking in the background will have a shot to nab him.

articles.title: Dolphins rookie WR still confident he'll show out despite slow start
articles.summary: The Dolphins took a receiver with first-round talent in the third round of this year's draft, and while he's had a slow start, he can still be great.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver Chris Bell was having a great final season at Louisville, catching 72 passes for 917 yards and six touchdowns before he tore his ACL in a late-November matchup against SMU that the Cardinals lost 38-6.

Now, nearly a full year after the injury, Bell is battling another knee ailment that kept him out of the team's Week 10 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. However, he isn't concerned about it going forward.

"It was nothing that really hurt me," Bell told reporters on Thursday. "I'm good. It was just a little hyperextension, nothing too serious."

While he missed the offseason recovering from the torn ACL, the 22-year-old returned to the field in time for the season opener, but his NFL career has started slowly, catching just 12 passes for 148 yards in his eight games.

Things haven't gone the way he would like so far this year, but he feels that he'll still prove himself to be a reliable weapon in Miami's offense.

"I ain't going to lie," Bell said. "Nobody has seen the real Chris Bell yet.... "It takes time to get back from an ACL. I didn't know that until going through this journey. Before I came back, I was hoping to go back out there and ball. I've got to work my way back into who I am. I am slowly getting back to myself."

In four years at Louisville, Bell caught 151 passes for 2,166 yards and 12 touchdowns. If he can return to the player he was before the ACL injury, the Dolphins will have gotten a steal in the third round, but he needs to show he can be that guy at this level.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso Calls Dakar Challenge ‘Another Level’
articles.summary: Fernando Alonso says the Dakar rally is harder than Formula 1. He details the mental strain and the unknown terrain he faces in 2027.
articles.body:
Fernando Alonso says the Dakar rally is a much harder test than Formula 1 racing. He told reporters that the unknown nature of the event makes it "another level" of difficulty. For a second time, the Spanish driver will return to the Dakar rally thanks to Aston Martin's three-car lineup. His return comes after he finished third in the 2020 event while driving for Toyota.

Alonso explained the mental gap between racing on a known track and racing in the wild. In Formula 1, drivers repeat the same thing lap after lap to perfect their driving style. The Dakar rally requires constant improvising because drivers do not know what happens next. He noted that the eyes cannot blink for four or five hours during the race. The focus on not blinking caused him headaches during his first test days.

The route for the 2027 Dakar will run from Portugal to Morocco. Originally scheduled for Saudi Arabia, the event was moved because of regional instability. The event's relocation to new conditions increases the difficulty for drivers. Alonso said "And Dakar is to the unknown; every metre is new" when discussing the challenge, according to Formula1.com . He feels the task is bigger for him because he did not grow up in that type of racing.

With the Dreadnought, Aston Martin will make its debut in the event. This is a real-world competition version of a car the manufacturer designed for the new game "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4." Alonso will have Marc Coma as his co-driver for the upcoming race.

Alonso knows he faces a steep climb to win the title. Sebastian Loeb, likely the greatest rally driver in history, is his teammate. Loeb has tried to win the Dakar nine or 10 times and has not achieved the win yet. Alonso said "I think I was competitive" when he reflected on his 2020 performance.

He admitted he had a good six months of preparation and thousands of kilometres of driving before that race. He does not have that same amount of time or distance in his current schedule. Despite the lack of prep, Alonso says the big challenge is what makes the event appealing. He wants to attempt to win it one day in the future.

articles.summary: MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — Karl-Anthony Towns scored 17 of his 22 points in the first half and grabbed 12 rebounds against his former team to help the New York Knick...
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — Karl-Anthony Towns scored 17 of his 22 points in the first half and grabbed 12 rebounds against his former team to help the New York Knicks hang on and beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 102-99 on Thursday night.

Jalen Brunson had 21 points and seven assists and OG Anunoby added 15 points for the Knicks (9-6), who won their third straight game despite nearly squandering a 19-point, third-quarter lead and failing to score over the final 3:26.

Ayo Dosunmu cut the deficit to three with a 3-pointer with 2:34 remaining and would've tied it on the next possession with another swish from deep, but that didn't count because of a premature whistle for a shot clock violation. Replay review determined LaMelo Ball's jumper had grazed the rim.

Ball missed a tying 3-point attempt with 9.9 seconds left, and the Timberwolves couldn't get another shot off.

Jonathan Kuminga had 23 points for the Timberwolves (11-5) in his return from a two-game absence because of a bruised right shoulder. Ball had 15 points on 6-for-21 shooting.

Towns, who was traded to the Knicks in 2024 after nine years with the Timberwolves, is having another standout season as he seeks a contract extension . He was greeted loudly and warmly by the crowd before the game and brought his best again to Minnesota.

After losing his balance on a contested layup, Towns fell flat on his back next to his father, Karl Towns, who helped him up from his baseline seat.

Towns had 32 points and 20 rebounds for the Knicks in a 133-107 victory two years ago in his first game in Minnesota after the trade. Last season, he had 40 points and 13 rebounds in his return during a 115-104 defeat , his first to the Timberwolves.

articles.body: Magnus Carlsen took an unusual route to protecting his place at the top of world chess, forfeiting two games against Vladislav Artemiev before producing a must-win performance in the Fast Classic to secure his first victory in the format at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest on Thursday.The five-time world champion, competing for 17th place, turned a 3-9 deficit into an 11-9 match victory, winning the Fast Classic game to complete an extraordinary comeback. The result also lifted his live rating to 2804, keeping him above the coveted 2,800 Elo mark and retaining his world No. 1 status.Carlsen's rating and ranking were genuinely under threat. A draw against Artemiev in the Fast Classic would have taken his rating down to 2799, marking the first time in 17 years that he would have fallen below 2,800. A defeat, coupled with a win for Fabiano Caruana, would also have opened the door for the American to become world No. 1.Carlsen's forfeiting strategy sets up a must-win showdownAfter winning three of the four blitz games against Artemiev, Carlsen announced that he would only return for the Fast Classic game, forfeiting both rapid games and handing his opponent eight points.It was a calculated gamble that left him needing an eight-point victory in the final game to win the day's match. Artemiev took advantage of the forfeits to establish a 9-3 lead, putting Carlsen in a position where only victory would suffice.The Norwegian, however, was not particularly confident about his chances going into the decisive encounter."I hadn't won a game of classical chess the whole tournament and he's very solid," Carlsen told Norwegian broadcaster TV 2.The game began with a Ruy Lopez, with Artemiev initially holding his own. However, the Russian found himself in severe time trouble by move 21, having just one minute remaining compared to Carlsen's 26 minutes.Carlsen steadily increased the pressure. Artemiev defended resourcefully on the increment and sacrificed a pawn, a decision that was initially sound, but eventually cracked under the mounting pressure.The victory gave Carlsen his first Fast Classic win in 11 games in the format at the tournament and, more importantly, ensured his rating remained above 2,800.Praggnanandhaa wins as Giri takes final leadElsewhere, R Praggnanandhaa defeated Abhimanyu Mishra 12-8 in their match for 21st place. After the four blitz games were split, Praggnanandhaa won the first rapid game and drew the remaining rapid and Fast Classic encounters.Arjun Erigaisi endured a disappointing turnaround against Haik Martirosyan. After taking a 3.5-0.5 lead in blitz, Erigaisi lost 14.5-5.5 as Martirosyan fought back with a win and a draw in rapid before taking the Fast Classic game. R Vaishali also lost, going down 16-4 to Nodirbek Abdusattorov.In the final, Dutch Grandmaster Anish Giri edged Alireza Firouzja 11-9 on the opening day. Giri's advantage in blitz proved decisive after the players exchanged rapid victories and drew their Fast Classic game. He needs a win or a draw on Friday to claim the Budapest pilot title, while Firouzja must win to force an Armageddon tiebreak.Fabiano Caruana also moved ahead in the third-place match, taking an 11-9 lead over Maxime Vachier-Lagrave.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Francesc Núñez, sociólogo, sobre la Lotería de Navidad: "Rechazarlo supone romper una norma social no escrita de pertenencia"
articles.standfirst: El sociólogo de la UOC analiza la dimensión simbólica y comunitaria del sorteo navideño
articles.summary: El sociólogo de la UOC analiza la dimensión simbólica y comunitaria del sorteo navideño
articles.body: El sonido inconfundible de los bombos girando en el Teatro Real inaugura cada año una atmósfera festiva que trasciende el mero ámbito económico. Para comprender por qué esta tradición del Sorteo Extraordinario de la Lotería de Navidad conserva intacta su fuerza en la sociedad actual, es necesario observar su dimensión cultural y simbólica más allá del dinero en juego. Al reflexionar sobre el valor ritual y simbólico del sorteo en la cultura contemporánea española, el sociólogo de la Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) Francesc Núñez destaca su papel determinante como pistoletazo de salida emocional de las fiestas. "El sorteo del 22 de diciembre funciona como un auténtico ritual colectivo que marca la entrada emocional en la Navidad", señala el investigador al analizar este fenómeno social. Este acontecimiento logra detener la rutina habitual e instaurar una serie de códigos compartidos que millones de ciudadanos reconocen al instante. Desde los hogares hasta los puestos de trabajo, la jornada adquiere un ritmo propio marcado por imágenes y sonidos que se repiten generación tras generación. "Tiene una liturgia muy reconocible: los niños de San Ildefonso, la retransmisión televisiva de fondo mientras trabajamos o desayunamos, el descorche de cava en las administraciones", describe Núñez sobre los elementos que vertebran esta celebración cotidiana en toda España. La fuerza de esta costumbre es tal que logra involucrar incluso a quienes habitualmente se mantienen al margen de cualquier juego de azar, convirtiendo el décimo en un símbolo de integración social. "Incluso las personas que se consideran racionales y que jamás pisan una casa de apuestas participan en este sorteo porque rechazarlo supone romper una norma social no escrita de pertenencia y celebración compartida", concluye el experto.

articles.title: Sandpapergate: Australian gov’t demands CA to ensure transparency in forum
articles.summary: Cricket Australia’s Sandpapergate forum for players to give their accounts has been ridiculed by former cricketers.
articles.body:
Cricket Australia (CA) should ensure its forum into Sandpapergate is handled as independently and openly as possible, a government spokesperson said on Friday, as former players slammed the governing body’s attempts to defuse an escalating controversy surrounding ⁠the 2018 ball-tampering scandal .

CA bosses said on Wednesday that an independent forum would be set up to allow players to give their accounts of the incident, but the results would not necessarily be made public and no sanctions would follow.

The move has been ridiculed by past players and pundits, ⁠including former captain Michael Clarke, who said the Australian public had been lied to about who was party to the cheating during the 2018 South Africa Test series.

A spokesperson for Sport Minister Anika Wells said integrity mattered to “every kid with a bat or a ball”.

“This is Cricket Australia’s process to run and it is a matter for them to work through. Australians will expect this to be run independently and as openly as possible,” the spokesperson ‌said in a statement.

“We have a summer of cricket to look forward to and I’m sure all of Australia will get behind our team.”

CA did not provide immediate comment when asked by the Reuters news agency on Friday for more details about its forum.

The eight-year-old Sandpapergate scandal has reignited this month following allegations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja that other players and staff knew of the ball-tampering – not just the three who were found culpable and sanctioned after a rapid investigation by CA’s integrity unit during the South Africa tour.

CA banned then-captain Steve Smith and David Warner for 12 months, and Cameron Bancroft for nine.

Test captain Pat Cummins and fellow ⁠pace bowler Mitchell Starc have since rejected Khawaja’s allegations , saying they had no prior knowledge of ball tampering.

But three ⁠other players involved in the 2018 tour came forward to back up Khawaja’s account, including Warner and Bancroft, who said “the whole team” knew , including coaching staff and a media manager.

Bancroft claimed the idea to rough up the ball with sandpaper to make it swing was Warner’s, but that the conversation had taken place “within a wider team environment”. He added that he had lied about the extent of the plot to protect CA’s investigation into the incident.

Clarke, who captained Australia from 2011 to 2015, said Bancroft’s explosive 4,000-word statement shared with the media on Wednesday had made CA’s forum redundant.

“The public don’t want any more bullshit,” ⁠he said on his podcast, Beyond23.

“The public want the complete truth to allow us to move on.”

The scandal has heaped pressure on Cummins, one of the game’s most devastating pace bowlers, who boasts a strong portfolio of ⁠corporate sponsors.

Cummins called Khawaja’s allegations “complete and utter nonsense” in an hour-long news conference last ⁠week, and criticised his former teammate for being “casual” with others’ lives and reputations.

He declined to comment to a large media scrum camped outside his Sydney home on Thursday and at training, but his manager said Cummins’s position remained steadfast and he had no need to respond to Bancroft’s statement.

A poll of 13,000 readers of Melbourne’s Herald Sun newspaper had 82 percent saying ‌they believed Khawaja’s, Warner’s and Bancroft’s accounts of Sandpapergate, versus 18 percent for Cummins and Australia’s bowlers who denied prior knowledge.

A majority of 6,000 readers in a poll in the Sydney Morning Herald said they did not expect Cummins to remain as captain for the first Test of the ‌home ‌summer against New Zealand, which starts December 9.

Former Australia bowler Mitchell Johnson said the public pressure on Cummins to stand down as captain would be too much.

“I just can’t see how his captaincy and personal brand survives this,” Johnson wrote in a column for The West Australian newspaper.

articles.title: Lamborghini Temerario Spyder: así es esta 'bestia' descapotable con 920 CV que alcanza 343 km/h
articles.standfirst: Lamborghini convierte su nuevo superdeportivo híbrido en descapotable. Conserva los 920 CV del Temerario Coupé y, para nuestra sorpresa, estrena un techo rígido que se pliega en vertical detrás de los asientos
articles.summary: Lamborghini convierte su nuevo superdeportivo híbrido en descapotable. Conserva los 920 CV del Temerario Coupé y, para nuestra sorpresa, estrena un techo rígido que se pliega en vertical detrás de los asientos
articles.body: Lamborghini ya tiene una nueva forma de disfrutar del Temerario. Llega bajo la denominación Spyder, y como su nombre indica prescinde del techo para dejar a la vista el cielo y, de paso, para que el sonido de su motor V8 llegue con menos filtros a los ocupantes. Y esto último no parece una mala idea cuando hablamos de un motor que puede rugir a más de 10.000 rpm. Pero lo más curioso en un coche de esta categoría está en su techo, que es rígido escamoteable. A juzgar por las imágenes, el Temerario Spyder conserva el atractivo y la personalidad del modelo cerrado, aunque la transformación no se limita a cortar el techo y reforzar después la carrocería. De hecho, Lamborghini ha rediseñado la zona posterior para integrar el mecanismo de apertura y dos prominentes elementos aerodinámicos situados detrás de los asientos, que vistos de lado prolongan el habitáculo hacia la zaga. Con el techo puesto mantiene una silueta parecida a la del cerrado; sin él, el conjunto adquiere una apariencia todavía más baja y musculosa. Pero centrémonos en el techo, que es lo más llamativo de esta versión y está formado por dos piezas que se pliegan en posición vertical detrás de los ocupantes, en lugar de hacerlo en horizontal, como sucede en otros descapotables. El sistema está operado por diez pequeños motores y permite guardar la capota en una posición muy baja y próxima al centro de gravedad del coche. Según Lamborghini, con el techo abierto el centro de gravedad desciende 3 mm, sin modificar casi la distribución de pesos entre los dos ejes. Por supuesto, ha habido que trabajar en la rigidez del chasis para compensar la desaparición del techo de la versión cerrada. Por ello, en Lamborghini aseguran que el Temerario Spyder mejora un 6% la rigidez torsional respecto al Huracán Spyder, lo que demuestra que en la marca italiana no se han tomado a broma su rendimiento en curvas o incluso en circuito. El sistema de propulsión es el mismo que el del Temerario Coupé. El protagonista es un V8 biturbo de 4,0 litros que entrega por sí solo 800 CV y puede alcanzar 10.250 rpm. Pero en asociación con este trabajan tres motores eléctricos, uno situado entre el motor de combustión y el cambio automático de doble embrague y ocho velocidades, y otros dos instalados en el eje delantero. Entre los cuatro, la potencia conjunta alcanza los 920 CV y el par máximo llega a 800 Nm. Con esta configuración híbrida enchufable y tracción total, el Temerario Spyder acelera de 0 a 100 km/h en 2,8 segundos y alcanza los 200 km/h desde parado en 7,3 segundos, todo ello coronado por una desorbitada velocidad máxima de 343 km/h. Es decir, entra por la puerta grande en el territorio de los superdeportivos descapotables más rápidos del planeta. Pero no todo tiene que ser ir a ritmo vertiginoso, porque el conductor puede elegir entre distintos modos de conducción y estrategias del sistema híbrido. En modo Città, el coche puede circular en eléctrico con hasta 190 CV; en Strada se priorizan el confort y la eficiencia, mientras que solo en Sport y Corsa se pueden disfrutar de los 920 CV. Y si más que disfrutar, se busca divertirsión en circuito, también cuenta con un modo Drift con tres niveles de intervención para que deslice más o menos del eje trasero en curvas. Para quienes ya se imaginan conduciéndolo con tranquilidad por la Costa Azul, este Spyder ofrece la posibilidad de regular la apertura de la luneta posterior (manteniendo el techo cerrado) para controlar la entrada de aire y el sonido del motor en el habitáculo. Además, los asientos pueden incorporar un sistema de calefacción para la zona del cuello, con tres grados de intensidad, pensado para poder circular a cielo abierto incluso cuando la temperatura no acompaña. Pero la marca italiana también ofrecerá el Temerario Spyder con una configuración aligerada, denominada Alleggerita, más orientada a quienes busquen sacar partido al coche en circuito. Incluye numerosos componentes de fibra de carbono, entre ellos el splitter delantero, los faldones laterales y el capó posterior. Si a ello le sumamos las llantas de carbono opcionales, el ahorro de peso alcanza los 22 kg respecto al Spyder convencional. Lo que Lamborghini no ha comunicado todavía es el precio ni la fecha en la que puede llegar a los concesionarios este nuevo descapotable.

articles.title: Loida Zabala: "He propuesto a los médicos que me amputen el pie"
articles.standfirst: La halterófila paralímpica, que lucha contra el cáncer desde 2023 pero está más fuerte que nunca, visita MARCA antes de competir en el Mundial de halterofilia
articles.summary: La halterófila paralímpica, que lucha contra el cáncer desde 2023 pero está más fuerte que nunca, visita MARCA antes de competir en el Mundial de halterofilia
articles.body: Loida Zabala entra en la redacción de MARCA con su perenne sonrisa. No la borra ni cuando habla de su estado de salud. "No quiero volver a tener esa sepsis por la que puedo perder la vida. He propuesto a los médicos amputarme el pie (derecho) como solución y esperemos que se pueda cumplir. Prefiero morir de cáncer dentro de unos años que ahora por sepsis", dice. Y vuelve a sonreír. Su entereza impresiona. Habla con mucha serenidad, pero a la vez desprende vitalidad y energía. La halterófila paralímpica, a la que diagnosticaron en 2023 un cáncer de pulmón con metástasis en cerebro y varios órganos más, estuvo ingresada en la UCI del Hospital Ramón y Cajal (Madrid) tres veces entre marzo y junio por una sepsis. "Tuve la suerte de que me salvaran la vida. Hoy tengo que seguir pendiente todo el rato de la tensión -entonces tenía de alta 50 y de baja 30-, pero no lo viví con miedo, preocupación o tristeza. Estaba con ocho sanitarios a mi alrededor y lo viví como espectadora. Me dejé fluir porque no era algo que dependiese de mí. Al final sobreviví", cuenta. Debido a los tratamientos oncológicos, Zabala tiene las defensas bajas y en marzo una bacteria provocó una infección en su pie derecho que se complicó y estuvo a punto de costarle la vida. "No sabes la escabechina que tengo ahí abajo", confiesa sonriendo de nuevo. Ha tenido que volver a Urgencias recientemente un par de veces. La solución para combatir las bacterias es dejar el tratamiento oncológico para que así le suban las defensas, pero la vigente subcampeona de Europa (de -73 Kg) no está dispuesta, de ahí que sea ella misma quien haya propuesto la amputación. Y pese a los problemas de salud, la extremeña sigue entrenando y logrando sus mejores marcas. "Antes del diagnóstico del cáncer nunca había levantado más de 100 kilos en una competición. Justo antes de la sepsis levanté 105 en el Europeo. Pero es que después de los tres ingresos pensé que no iba a levantar más de 90 y hace poco llegué 113 en el gimnasio", revela. ¿Y cuál es el secreto? Le preguntamos. "Es muy importante generar oxitocina con la gente que tienes alrededor y las endorfinas haciendo deporte. He llegado al mejor punto de mi vida cuando peor salud tengo. Cada mañana lo primero que pienso es que estoy viva, que tengo la oportunidad de seguir viviendo y es el mejor regalo que tenemos", reflexiona. El deporte es su mejor medicina. "Me da la vida", asegura, porque no sólo le ayuda a nivel físico sino también emocional y psíquico. "La primera vez que me dieron el diagnóstico de cáncer me dijeron que no podía entrenar porque tenía nueve tumores en el cerebro. A los dos meses ya pude y eso es lo que me hizo volver a ser independiente porque había perdido la fuerza incluso para pasarme a la bañera", cuenta. El día 30 de noviembre competirá en el Mundial en Bahrein (11:35h) -también la española Montse Alcoba (11:25h)- con el objetivo de levantar 110 kilos. "Es una cantidad con la que ni siquiera soñaba en 2023, lo que pasa es que ahora veo tan fuerte... Vamos a seguir aprovechando que mi punto de salud está bien para hacer las mejores marcas porque a los Juegos de Los Ángeles van las ocho mejores del mundo. Voy a dar todo lo que pueda de mí para mantenerme clasificada", asegura. Serían sus sextos Juegos. No ha faltado a ninguno desde Pekín 2008. Y, además, Los Ángeles para ella es especial. "Conocí a mi pareja jugando al Grand Theft Auto V, que es el mapa de esa ciudad. Para mí ir a allí, a Los Juegos, con él sería muy bonito", reconoce. Y en el camino hacia LA2028 está viviendo con intensidad cada momento. "Ahora vivo cada día pensando en el presente. Es un sueño llegar a Los Ángeles y llegar viva", dice. He hecho un pacto con mi oncóloga y ojalá podamos cumplirlo. Ya no celebro mi cumpleaños real (5 de abril) sino el aniversario del diagnóstico del cáncer (28 de octubre), mi súper cumple”, confiesa Ahora ya no cuento mi cumpleaños real (5 de abril), sino el aniversario del diagnóstico del cáncer (28 de octubre) y celebro mi súper cumple", dice, cómo no, sonriendo. Porque Loida no tiene miedo a nada.

articles.title: Kenya’s growing doping crisis overshadows legacy as athletics powerhouse
articles.summary: More than 140 Kenyan athletes suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit since 2017, most of them distance runners.
articles.body:
Over decades, Kenya built a legacy of producing elite runners who dominated distance running. The recipe for success was simple: High-altitude training, a whole-foods diet, early nights, consistency.

But a quiet, underhanded addition over the past few years is threatening to tarnish its legacy and the dozens of global accolades that stemmed from it – doping.

The African nation’s latest doping scandal is perhaps the most shocking; Peres Jepchirchir, world and Olympic marathon champion, was handed a three-year ban on Thursday for testing positive for banned blood booster EPO.

The Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said Jepchirchir’s sample was taken before her Sydney Marathon victory in August, where she stormed to her fourth World Marathon Majors win after triumph in New York (2021), Boston (2022), and London (2024). She’s also a former half-marathon world record holder.

Jepchirchir, who admitted to breaching anti-doping rules, is arguably the most prominent and successful in a string of Kenyan athletes who have faced formal doping sanctions over the past decade. Since 2017, more than 140 Kenyan athletes have been suspended by AIU, most of them distance runners.

How has Kenyan athletics ended up at this point and what comes next? Al Jazeera Sport spoke to experts to find out.

Why has there been a rise in doping violations among Kenyan runners?

Rather than seeing it as a rise, the reality is that more athletes are being tested, caught, and publicised for doping violations, former Kenyan middle-distance runner Martin Keino told Al Jazeera.

“Testing has expanded, particularly out-of-competition testing, and the AIU now goes after suspicious patterns instead of waiting for a positive sample,” said Keino, a former pacer who helped set seven world records.

“The problem is real, but the visibility is new.”

Financial insecurity, fear of decline in performance, and pressure to deliver are some of the biggest factors, Keino explained.

“Kenya produces a huge number of runners chasing a very small number of life-changing contracts. When one breakthrough can lift a whole family out of poverty, the pull to find an edge gets much stronger.

“Add weak local controls on banned substances, unqualified ‘coaches’ and agents who push for quick results, and doping can spread quietly.”

For Kenyan Olympic champion Wilfred Bungei, men’s 800m champion at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, the rise in doping violations hits closer to home.

Bungei is a relative veteran compared with contemporary Kenyan greats like Eliud Kipchoge , Sebastian Sawe and Faith Kipyegon , who have continued the legacy built by the likes of Martin’s father Kip Keino, one of Kenya’s first Olympic champions in the 1960s. He says doping violations by the likes of Jepchirchir and Ruth Chepngetich jeopardise the legitimacy of future victories while tarnishing the current legacy.

“For decades, Kenya has built its athletics on solid hard work from dedicated athletes. Now, some athletes are choosing the shortest way to make it big in athletics, by cheating,” Bungei said.

“I can only describe it as greed, selfishness and above all just plain stupidity to not understand that it’s not you the doper who is damaged but thousands of Kenyan athletes who built their careers on pure sweat and discipline.”

Caroline Mwanzia, an international sports lawyer practising in anti-doping, safeguarding, and sports governance, had a more straightforward view.

“For some athletes, it is because of intentionally wanting to gain an unfair advantage over other athletes competing,” she said.

“Others may have taken medicinal drugs without first obtaining a Therapeutic Use Exemption [TUE], but most athletes are simply being ignorant.”

Are athletes always at fault for doping violations?

This is where the lines get blurred on whether athletes or their support personnel are responsible for what goes into their bodies. Bungei insists that the responsibility “sits squarely on the athlete”.

“I don’t believe that an athlete with integrity would be encouraged by anyone to do what is wrong,” he said.

Keino held a similar sentiment. “Most elite athletes know the basics: The prohibited list, testing, whereabouts rules, the penalties. You can’t compete at World Marathon Major level and claim total ignorance of the rules.”

But knowing the rules is different from understanding every product, injection, supplement, or “recovery treatment” handed to you, Keino explained.

“Some athletes take things without really understanding the risks, the dosages, the detection windows, or who is supplying them. Others take banned substances knowingly and hide behind ignorance later.”

Per a 2016 investigation, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) found two Kenyan athletes who attempted to escape their sanctions by providing falsified medical records, one of which WADA termed the “culminating peak in an overall strategy of cover-up and concealment by the athlete”.

“That’s why education has to be practical. A seminar where someone reads out the WADA code isn’t enough,” Keino emphasised.

“Athletes need to hear it plainly: Never take an injection or unknown substance without checking it, keep records, ask questions, and walk away from any coach or agent who can’t explain what they’re giving you.”

WADA also concluded in its investigation that “athletes in Kenya are insufficiently educated on doping and/or wilfully blind as to the consequences of doping.”

Experience doesn’t make you immune to pressure, fear, or bad decisions, Keino explained.

“Established runners actually carry a different kind of pressure. They have a reputation to protect, a lifestyle to maintain, and people depending on them.

“An injury, a dip in form, or a few poor races can hit contracts, appearance fees, and sponsorship fast.”

Keino went on to explain that for veteran athletes like Jepchirchir and Chepngetich, doping is not to break into the elite circle but to stay on top longer, keep up with younger athletes, or bounce back from a setback.

“None of that excuses it – at that level, nobody can credibly say they don’t know what EPO is, how it works, or why it’s banned.”

Should Kenya be sanctioned by global bodies?

“Back in 2009 when a few doping cases had been reported, I advocated for the criminalisation of doping and people thought I was too harsh. Almost 20 years later, Kenya’s image is on the line,” said Bungei, who still believes the government should make doping a criminal offence in Kenya.

In September, Kenya signed the Anti-Doping Amendment Bill 2026 to align with WADA’s updated code, a decade after it was first signed into law after WADA declared Kenya non-compliant with global anti-doping rules and regulations.

“Better options [than sanctions] are stronger audits of Kenya’s anti-doping system, funding for testing and education, bans for repeat enablers, and conditions attached to hosting major events,” Keino said.

“Nairobi’s award of the 2029 World Athletics Championships should come with real accountability, not just prestige.”
