articles.title: Drone operator removes Man United training footage and issues apology
articles.summary: The footage, filmed during new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session, was uploaded online.
articles.body:
A drone operator who filmed Manchester United’s ⁠training session ⁠this week has apologised for what he called a “total error of judgement” and removed the footage from ⁠his YouTube channel.

The footage, filmed at United’s Carrington training ground during new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session on ⁠Thursday, was uploaded online under the username “CC OVERVIEW”.

In a statement posted on his YouTube channel on Friday, the drone operator said that while the flight was legal under drone regulations, filming ‌the session had been “unethical”.

“My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time,” he said.

“I fully accept it was unethical on my part. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players ⁠for my actions and sincerely hope those ⁠actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”

The operator added that he had wrongly assumed only warm-up activities would be visible and that ⁠the training session would be open to various media outlets.

He also said neither Liverpool ⁠nor any other football club had been ⁠involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he said.

Pochettino arrived from the US men’s national team this ‌week after United sacked Michael Carrick , and faces an immediate test with a trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

United are ‌languishing ‌18th in the league table after winning just one of their 10 games. Liverpool are fourth.

articles.title: Kevin Viñuela redondea su actuación en Abu Dabi con una plata mundial
articles.standfirst: El júnior Damián Suárez fue bronce, mientras que la victoria se la adjudicó el británico Christopher Perham
articles.summary: El júnior Damián Suárez fue bronce, mientras que la victoria se la adjudicó el británico Christopher Perham
articles.body: El triatleta leonés Kevin Tarek Viñuela ha redondeado su actuación en el campeonato del mundo de multideportes que se disputa en Abu Dabi con la medalla de plata en la prueba de acuatlón, su segunda presea en la cita mundialista tras el bronce en la modalidad de Triatlón Cross. Viñuela, subió un escalón en el podio en detrimento de otro de los representantes españoles, el júnior Damián Suárez, que fue subcampeón mundial el pasado año en Pontevedra. La victoria se decidió en el segundo tramo de carrera de 2.700 metros, tras el segmento de mil metros en el agua con el británico Christopher Perham, que se presentaba como uno de los favoritos, se acabó imponiendo con un tiempo de 30:27, con Kevin Tarek a 10 segundos, aventajando en un apretado esprint a Suárez que cerró el podio, con los rusos Grigory Antipov y Pavel Sorokin por detrás. El tercer español en la prueba, Jonay Álvarez, que había sido en el Lago de Banyoles el pasado mes de julio campeón de Europa con tan solo 18 años, fue sexto, y descalificado al no detenerse en la zona de penalización para cumplir una sanción de 15 segundos. En categoría femenina, Marina Muñoz, que el pasado martes logró el oro mundial de triatlón cross, salió del agua en tercera posición encabezando el grupo perseguidor, pero sin opciones de acercarse a las medallas -acabó sexta- que fueron para la rusa Valentina Riasova con un tiempo de 34:37, con Margot Garabedian, de Camboya, plata a 3 segundos, y la también rusa Iana Chenskaia bronce un segundo después.

articles.title: Maria Laura Ferreya, la jugadora de pádel con hipoacusia que aprendió a escuchar con los ojos
articles.standfirst: Esta jugadora argentina, que nació con hipoacusia, ha aprendido a convivir con ella, utiliza audífonos durante sus partidos y ha disputado el Mundial en 2026.
articles.summary: Esta jugadora argentina, que nació con hipoacusia, ha aprendido a convivir con ella, utiliza audífonos durante sus partidos y ha disputado el Mundial en 2026.
articles.body: Hay cosas que en una pista de pádel se escuchan. Un aviso de la compañera, una indicación durante un punto o una llamada que puede evitar que dos jugadoras vayan a por la misma pelota. Pero también hay cosas que se aprenden a percibir de otra manera. María Laura Ferreyra (Villa Ángela, Argentina 2005) lo sabe bien. Nació con hipoacusia y, con el paso de los años, ha desarrollado una forma propia de interpretar lo que sucede a su alrededor. “Con los ojos he aprendido a ‘escuchar’ cosas también”, explica. Su historia con el deporte comenzó con una raqueta de tenis. A los siete años la hipoacusia que la acompañaba desde el nacimiento le fue diagnosticada oficialmente. Tres años después, a los diez, cambió el tenis por el pádel. Desde entonces, ha aprendido a desenvolverse en una disciplina en la que la comunicación con la compañera puede resultar determinante. La hipoacusia es la pérdida de capacidad auditiva y puede presentarse en distintos grados, desde leve hasta profunda, y afectar a uno o ambos oídos. Según la Organización Mundial de la Salud más de 1.500 millones de personas en el mundo viven con algún grado de pérdida auditiva y alrededor de 430 millones necesitan servicios de rehabilitación por una pérdida auditiva discapacitante. Una realidad amplia y diversa que también tiene su reflejo en el deporte de alto nivel aunque la experiencia de cada deportista sea diferente. Ferreyra utiliza audífonos durante sus partidos y en todo momento y aun así hay situaciones en las que escuchar resulta más que complicado. “Mirar a mi compañera de frente me facilita más las cosas”, explica. Cuando ejecuta una bajada de pared y queda de espaldas, le cuesta más percibir sus indicaciones. “Tuve que aprender a competir con esto", reconoce y cuya adaptación forma parte de su rutina. Entrena y compite con normalidad y, con 21 años, ocupa el puesto 76 del ranking FIP y puede presumir de haber ganado el FIP Silver de Dubái junto a su compañera actual Anna Ortiz. Su experiencia no consiste en que las dificultades hayan desaparecido, sino en haber aprendido a convivir con ellas y encontrar su propia manera de interpretar el juego. La adaptación también deja momentos que, vistos desde fuera, pueden resultar tan sorprendentes como divertidos. Ferreyra recuerda una situación que vivió durante un encuentro en la que cuando estaba disputando un punto se le cayeron los audífonos. Terminó la jugada y comenzó a buscarlos. Mientras ella intentaba recuperar los dispositivos, el resto de las personas presentes no entendía qué estaba pasando. "No se cantó let porque nadie se dio cuenta, solo yo sabía lo que buscaba”, cuenta entre risas. La anécdota también abre una cuestión reglamentaria. El artículo 6.6.2 de las reglas de la Federación Internacional de Pádel (FIP) contempla las interferencias involuntarias, como la caída de una pelota del bolsillo o de una gorra, y establece que la primera vez debe sancionarse un let. Sin embargo, el texto no menciona específicamente los audífonos, por lo que no puede darse por sentado que su caída reciba exactamente el mismo tratamiento. Lo que queda claro es que Ferreyra no quiere que la hipoacusia ocupe todo el espacio de su historia. “Para mí esto no es un problema, lo tengo 100% normalizado”, afirma. Su manera de entenderlo no pasa por presentar cada dificultad como una batalla, sino por asumirla como parte de su vida y seguir adelante. Más allá de su experiencia personal, Ferreyra tiene objetivos deportivos que van mucho más allá de la hipoacusia. Uno de los motivos de alegría de esta temporada ha sido su convocatoria con la selección argentina para el Mundial de Pádel 2026, en el que terminó como subcampeona del mundo tras caer en la final ante España. “No me esperaba estar convocada, pero estoy muy feliz”, confiesa de un camino en el que, por suerte, también tiene referentes claros y entre ellos está Delfina Brea, número 1 del mundo, y una de las grandes figuras del pádel argentino y ahora su compañera de equipo. Para sostener una carrera profesional, además, señala dos pilares que considera imprescindibles: “Un buen equipo y el apoyo de la familia". Detrás de cada partido hay entrenamientos, decisiones, sacrificios y personas que acompañan el proceso, también en los momentos menos visibles. La historia de María Laura Ferreyra no necesita convertir la hipoacusia en una barrera insuperable ni en una ventaja extraordinaria. Su experiencia habla de aprendizaje, adaptación y normalidad. De una jugadora que ha encontrado su manera de competir, que sabe dónde puede encontrar más dificultades y que ha aprendido a interpretar la pista también con la mirada. Porque en el pádel hay información que llega a través del oído, pero no todo se decide por lo que se escucha. A veces, como demuestra Ferreyra, también se aprende a escuchar con los ojos.

articles.title: “I haven’t cheated the game”: Why William Nylander’s Toronto Maple Leafs demotion raises questions about Auston Matthews amid NHL concerns
articles.summary: Toronto Maple Leafs winger William Nylander's recent demotion raises questions about his role and Auston Matthews' leadership as the team faces a tough stretch. Fans are concerned about the team's performance and accountability issues ahead of their game against the Los Angeles Kings.
articles.body: William Nylander, a winger for the Toronto Maple Leafs, has reportedly been demoted in the lineup, raising questions about his role as the team struggles. The forward skated with Dakota Joshua and Nikita Tverberg at Thursday’s morning skate, a departure from the normal top-six role for the forward.The move comes amid speculation of increasing frustration involving Nylander and captain Auston Matthews. As the Toronto Maple Leafs prepare to play the Los Angeles Kings, Nylander’s comments after practice have added another layer to the conversation.Why William Nylander’s demotion raises questions about Auston MatthewsWilliam Nylander's reported move to a lower line has become a major talking point for the Toronto Maple Leafs, especially given the team's recent performances and the timing of his comments.Nylander was reportedly skating with Dakota Joshua and Nikita Tverberg during the team's morning skate on Thursday, November 19. The change represents a considerable adjustment for the Swedish forward, who has generally been an important part of Toronto's top-six offensive group.The coaching staff has not publicly explained the reason for the reported lineup change, but the move could be a bid to change the team’s offensive combinations or to get a better response from its players.Toronto has been dealing with a difficult losing stretch, making lineup changes increasingly important as the organization looks for ways to regain momentum. Moving an established offensive contributor into a different role can also be a way to create competition and generate a response from the rest of the roster.Nylander's comments following Thursday's practice attracted additional attention because they came shortly after the reported lineup change.The forward defended his approach to the game, stating:“I don’t think I’ve cheated the game this season. Probably the least I’ve cheated the game. I’ve got an opportunity to battle at the goal line. We still have some time to get back.”How are Auston Matthews' comments connected?The timing of Nylander's response has also brought Auston Matthews into the conversation. Earlier comments from the Toronto Maple Leafs captain reportedly highlighted concerns about issues that surfaced during the team's previous game against the Chicago Blackhawks.The similarity in the broader discussion surrounding accountability and competing at the goal line has encouraged fans to examine whether the two players share the same assessment of Toronto's recent performances.What does the Los Angeles Kings game mean?Toronto Maple Leafs have a great opportunity to respond to their recent losing streak when they take on the Los Angeles Kings in the next game.A good performance could take some of the heat off the team and put the focus back on results, rather than specific lineup decisions.Nylander's role will also be worth monitoring, particularly whether the coaching staff retains his reported new line combination or restores him to a more familiar offensive position.The goal for Matthews and the rest of the Toronto roster is to find consistency and pick up some valuable points.The reported demotion, Nylander's comments and the speculation surrounding Matthews have created an additional storyline for the Maple Leafs. But the games against the teams ahead will be a better barometer of whether the changes made can get Toronto back on track.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Newcastle United vs Arsenal: Premier League – Predictions, lineups, preview
articles.summary: As players return from international break, Premier League leaders Arsenal face Newcastle away on match day 11.
articles.body:
Who : Newcastle United vs Arsenal What : Premier League, match day 11 Where : St James’ Park, Newcastle, United Kingdom When : Saturday, November 21, at 5:30pm (17:30 GMT). How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 14:30 GMT before our live text commentary stream.

Club football returns this weekend following the international break, with Premier League leaders Arsenal looking to pick up where they left off in Saturday’s trip to Newcastle United.

The Gunners defeated Hull City 1-0 in their last league game before the break, extending their winning streak to five games after a promising start to their title defence.

The star-studded trio of Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka have kept the red half of North London happy with their combined nine league goals. But Mikel Arteta’s side will once again have to do without their injured winger Saka for the upcoming test at St James’ Park.

Newcastle, on the other hand, come into this game on the back of a 1-1 draw with Fulham and eager to get back to winning ways.

Anthony Elanga, Harvey Barnes and Joe Willock have been the most prolific goalscorers for the Magpies, who are winless in three games.

Arsenal are the best performers in the Premier League this season.

After 10 games, the Gunners lead the table with 27 points, with nine wins and one defeat.

They have a five-point lead over second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion, and six points more than third-placed Manchester City.

Newcastle are in the bottom half of the table, sitting 12th with 12 points.

The Magpies have won three games, drawn three and lost four.

What happened when Arsenal and Newcastle last met?

The teams last met in the Premier League on April 25. Arsenal won 1-0 that day at the Emirates Stadium, thanks to a ninth-minute thunderbolt from Eberechi Eze.

Opta’s supercomputer has picked Arsenal as the favourites.

Arsenal are predicted to have a 56.4 percent chance of winning, while Newcastle’s odds of victory are 21.7 percent. There is a 21.9 percent probability of a draw on Saturday.

(Last five Premier League matches; latest game first)

Brazilian midfielder Joelinton, who has not featured since the start of this month, is doubtful with a knock, while full-back Tino Livramento is available.

“I don’t want to be too precise with the medical update. We will get feedback from the specialists and we will find out how long Joe will be out,” coach Matthias Jaissle said about Joelinton.

“We had nine injuries – now most of them are back; slowly but surely we will get them back to match fitness,” the manager added. “We need to be patient with them. It gives us flexibility.”

Lukas Hornicek; Amar Dedic, Malick Thiaw, Dan Burn, Lewis Hall; Sean Steur, Lewis Miley, Jacob Murphy, Yoane Wissa, Harvey Barnes; William Osula

Defender William Saliba is set to return from a long injury layoff that has kept him out since the 2026 World Cup semifinals in July.

But winger Saka is expected to remain out for another month with a thigh injury.

“We had another test,” said Arteta on Friday. “[Saka] is evolving really well but looks like it’s going to be an eight-week injury, more or less, so I think it’s four at the moment, so it’s a while for him to be back with the team.”

Midfielder Martin Zubimendi picked up a hamstring injury on international duty last week, and Arteta said he would be out for a “few weeks”, while youngster Max Dowman is serving a suspension.

articles.title: Don't Expect The Rock to Use WWE Survivor Series to Set Up Roman Reigns Match at WrestleMania 43
articles.summary: During an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, The Rock announced that he will return at WWE Survivor Series: WarGames, creating speculation about what this means for WrestleMania season.
articles.body:
During an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show , The Rock announced that he will return at WWE Survivor Series: WarGames, creating speculation about what this means for WrestleMania season.

It's that time of year again. Every year, the WWE Universe hopes The Most Electrifying Man in Sports Entertainment will reemerge to deliver one last dream match.

As such, The Rock vs. Roman Reigns has reached mythical status. It's the what-if that fans just can't stop talking about. Rumors of this generational matchup first surfaced in 2018 , but it came so close to happening in 2024 that it almost seemed inevitable.

However, he opposed Cody Rhodes as The Final Boss instead, and the two-time Royal Rumble winner faced Reigns on night two of WrestleMania 40. At the event, The American Nightmare finished the story, but fans still anticipated a battle between the biggest stars of their eras.

After two years, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia seems like a logical destination for such a blockbuster match because its government-sponsored events have drawn so many big-name celebrities. Still, everything about this announcement would suggest otherwise.

Straight away, it's a bit bizarre that The Rock would make such an announcement the week before Survivor Series. This certainly isn't the first time he has done something like this, but it's not how WWE conventionally promotes its premium live events.

The 30th anniversary of his debut at the event is a momentous occasion. You would think the company would want to sell more tickets to coincide with this and his long-awaited return.

According to Wrestlevotes Radio of Fightful Select , "WWE had no traditional digital media advertising prepared to promote Rock's appearance, as the news had caught many within the company off guard. Those we spoke to in the merchandising division indicated that Rock/Survivor Series merch had not been finalized, or, if it had, the plans and concepts were being kept extremely confidential."

The report went on to say, "It is not believed that The Rock will be wrestling anytime soon. However, considering the nature of this surprise announcement, things can certainly change."

It's a curious situation. Long-time fans will likely see this as a ploy to keep them guessing, but this also fits his routine over the last three years. His appearances have been so erratic and spontaneous that it's tough to determine his intentions.

More to the point, the apparent power struggle makes it easy to believe that many people within the company found out about his return when we did. The Rock has used The Pat McAfee Show to disseminate information before, and it seemed just as impromptu.

Nostalgia will keep many viewers' hopes alive, but The Final Boss was so entertaining that most of us would like to see The Rock on the road to WrestleMania 43. Honestly, the prospect of him showing up to disrupt WWE's plans again is also quite amusing.

There are so many options for intriguing storylines involving Reigns, The Bloodline, or Rhodes. This would also be the ideal time to start setting up his return to The Grandest Stage of Them All.

Nevertheless, we've been here before, and it's hard to keep getting invested in a match that is becoming less realistic. We don't even know if The Rock has time to get in shape to compete in a match of that caliber with his hectic schedule.

If The Great One can get back in ring shape, what would the match even look like at this point? Can it possibly live up to all the hype?

Considering Reigns' output this year, this is the best time to capitalize on this once-in-a-lifetime matchup. After all, The Tribal Chief has vanquished the ghosts from his past and silenced some critics. He defeated CM Punk at The Showcase of the Immortals and scored a definitive win over Seth Rollins at SummerSlam.

Moreover, Reigns has successfully defended the World Heavyweight Championship all year without any outside interference. Beating The Rock would be the last win he needs to cement his legacy.

A highly anticipated showdown with Oba Femi seems more likely, though. It's safe to assume Survivor Series will be business as usual for The Rock, a quick stop to give the fans a moment and promote his next movie.

Yes, anything is possible, but don't expect more than that. Temper your expectations because nothing about this announcement resembles a return to wrestling.

articles.title: 10 Booking Moves Triple H and WWE Must Make to Save SmackDown
articles.summary: There was a time not that long ago that SmackDown was WWE's top show, highlighted by the must-see Bloodline angles.
articles.body:
There was a time not that long ago that SmackDown was WWE's top show, highlighted by the must-see Bloodline angles.

However, after Netflix won the right to Raw into 2025, WWE put all the focus on the red brand, making it easily WWE's most important weekly show.

Multiple big names were pulled over to Raw, especially Roman Reigns, leaving SmackDown looking less important.

Even worse for SmackDown was the attempt to make the show three hours long, leading to some of the worst episodes of television the company has produced in the last two years.

At this point, the star power balance between Raw and SmackDown is much thinner as both CM Punk and Cody Rhodes are working the blue brand. SmackDown is also keeping to two hours, for now.

This should have led to a smaller gap in quality between the two shows, but fans still clearly see Raw as the top show while SmackDown is secondary viewing.

Raw gets major themed nights and all of The Bloodline drama while SmackDown seems to be coasting on name value.

If this continues, it is highly likely SmackDown's value as a brand will be lower than it has ever been at the time of new media rights conversations.

How can WWE right the course? Here are 10 big booking decisions WWE must make right away to get SmackDown back on track.

Kevin Owens Should Dethrone Sami Zayn at Royal Rumble and Face Randy Orton at WrestleMania 43

Sami Zayn and Kevin Owens have been locked in an epic conflict that dates back to before WWE under different names.

At every stage, these two men have made the most of the spotlight and their history to deliver memorable matches time and again.

It would only be appropriate that the new two fight for the Undisputed WWE Championship sooner than later.

While SmackDown is already teasing this direction, the company has not set a clear path for Zayn's world title run into 2027.

Royal Rumble 2027 will be a massive show in Glendale, Arizona. It should be a night that WWE puts all of the world titles on the line on top of the classic Rumble matches.

KO can finally find his way back to the world title just about two years after he had to step away from the ring following a brutal Unsanctioned match against Zayn.

This is a chance to put everything back on track for Owens. He can become WWE champion and carry the title into 'Mania to face the man he was supposed to fight at WrestleMania 41.

Owens vs. Orton is clearly a match both men want and would give a strong foundation to SmackDown through 'Mania.

The narrative of The Viper seeking his 15th world title and Owens finally going to 'Mania as world champion will work much better than Cody Rhodes vs. Orton did last year.

It could even set up a double turn as Owens always enjoys a heel role more, and fans want to cheer The Viper to making history.

Keep At Least 4 Fresh Names Involved in the WWE Championship Scene at a Time

The best way to make a world title scene fresh is to keep a rotating list of stars that all want to be world champion.

At present, this is the best part of SmackDown where Sami Zayn is ducking Kevin Owens, Gunther, Trick Williams, Finn Bálor and even his own ally Johnny Gargano.

WWE should not lose track of any of these men wanting to be the top star, confronting Zayn as much as their current rivals.

This should not include Cody Rhodes or CM Punk, who can be placed in other rivalries outside of the title scene for a while.

Bring back Drew McIntyre and Randy Orton with world title aspirations, and the title scene will constantly look dynamic no matter who the champion is.

Move CM Punk Out of the Title Scene Into Rivalry with NXT Call-Up

CM Punk has teased turning his focus to NXT for a while lately, and fresh interactions with the young talent for Punk land much better than his world-title-adjacent feuds.

The Best in the World's current character is built on the knowledge that time is creeping up on him, and he can feel that even more if he is dealing with the future of WWE over returning to feuds with Cody Rhodes or Randy Orton.

NXT still has multiple names ready for a call-up. Tony D'Angelo in particular looks lost in NXT and could benefit from a call-up in the men's Royal Rumble match.

Why not immediately put him into conflict with Punk? The Best in the World can immediately test the limits of the former NXT champion and build him as a serious threat into WrestleMania 43.

Ideally, this feud could build Tony D up to his first 'Mania match of his career, facing Punk in a grudge match that will give him the best possible early spotlight on SmackDown.

Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico 🔮

Ranking WWE and AEW's Most Underrated Stars of 2026 🌟

Make Chelsea Green vs. Tiffany Stratton The Central Rivalry of SmackDown

Chelsea Green's first reign as WWE women's champion started to sell that she could be a legitimate star for the company going forward.

However, some bad in-ring pairings showed the faults in her game, leaving fans with questions of whether she will get back to the world title.

The betrayal of Tiffany Stratton gives Green a dynamic story that could carry SmackDown if WWE gives it the careful focus of a men's main event rivalry.

Even if Green's wrestling is inconsistent, she has absolutely nailed the promo work when asked, and she can lean into that as SmackDown's top babyface, still looking to prove her worth.

Tiffy is an obvious backstage favorite and can carry herself like one as champion. Make fans hate her arrogance and refusal to give Green credit.

The women's division has not had a story with this much potential juice in a while, but it will only work if WWE commits to the story and talent by giving them regular promo time and clear main event spotlights.

Pivot Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley Feud to Focus on Fatal Influence

Charlotte Flair vs. Jade Cargill is simply not working. Despite all attempts to make this the biggest story in the women's division, WWE has not established any reason to anticipate a memorable payoff.

The best answer would be to utilize the upcoming WarGames match to move the focus of Charlotte, Bliss and Paxley fully to Fatal Influence, especially Jacy Jayne's Women's United States Championship.

Jayne is the perfect type of star to carry the US title, but over her first 90 days as champion, she has defended her title just once on television, just the week after winning the gold.

She is approaching Liv Morgan numbers for lack of title defenses despite wrestling multiple times a month non-title.

The Queen, The Goddess and Tater could all give Jayne strong challenges for her title, especially with Fatal Influence protecting the champion along the way.

These title defenses can make the Women's United States Championship feel important again, and this trios rivalry would make so much more sense than the never-ending battle with The Baddies.

Since April 24, 2026, Blake Monroe has been a member of the SmackDown roster. She only finally made her in-ring debut on October 2, 2026.

She has only wrestled twice on SmackDown in 2026, both times against Giulia in October.

This is simply a waste of talent at a time when SmackDown needs more variety in its women's division.

Monoe ticks all the boxes for WWE, so why is she barely doing anything on SmackDown?

At the very least, Monroe should be wrestling or speaking in a ring most weeks to help establish herself as a threat.

Even losses to credible names would be more effective usage of The Glamour, who knows how to make the most of her time when she gets it.

Trade Giulia to Raw for Bayley to SmackDown

Giulia is a fantastic performer that could do more on SmackDown, but she is complete directionless.

A fresh start could do her well, and a trade of Giulia for Bayley would help SmackDown's women's division depth.

The Role Model is a reliable veteran that lose to anyone without losing credibility.

SmackDown can fully pair her up with her WarGames' partners Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley to form a strong women's stable.

Combined with the two previous slides, Blake Monroe could join Fatal Influence and create a strong stable war into 2027 that can bleed over to Raw as well in the battle for control of the Women's Tag Team Championship held by The Baddies.

What has become of SmackDown's men's tag team division?

The MFTs are a shell of their former selves with only Tama Tonga and Talla Tonga still standing.

While they hold tag gold, neither man comes off as a real threat to the SmackDown roster, holding the titles because their real competition is Bakusai.

It is time to create fresh teams to compete in this division. Why not take some of the lesser used names and pair them up?

Move Big Cass to SmackDown and pair him with Baron Corbin as a pair of bully big men. Let Rey Fénix and Chad Gable work SmackDown together.

Give Damian Priest a loudmouth ally in Ricky Saints. Can Sami Zayn and Johnny Gargano become a real tag team? As weird as it could get, let "The Demon" Finn Bálor and Danhausen terrorize the competition.

These are only some of the options to retool a tag division that could also use Angel and Berto as well as The Miz and Kit Wilson in more serious roles.

Depth is the biggest problem in this division, and there is no reason that everyone on SmackDown should not have an established ally to help them threaten the tag division.

Make Fraxiom the Next WWE Tag Team Championships

Once SmackDown has genuine depth in the tag team division, it will be important to establish a team that can work with absolutely everyone.

Tama Tonga and Talla Tonga are simply not interesting enough to serve that role.

The best answer is the team SmackDown continues to ignore: Fraxiom.

Axiom and Nathan Frazer are an established, exciting team that always delivers in the ring. They can work with absolutely anyone on SmackDown.

Fraxiom's recent return to NXT helped establish the new team of Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno, who would go onto win the 2026 Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic.

They can do that on SmackDown weekly, working with forgotten and new teams in frantic must-see matches.

Fraxiom are the obvious answer to SmackDown's tag team division woes, but WWE does not seem to see them.

The last booking need is the most obvious problem in WWE right now: Cody Rhodes.

The former top man of WWE is still popular, but he has struggled all year to deliver in the ring and on the mic despite a heavy spotlight.

His feuds with Randy Orton and Gunther were forgettable efforts that allowed Roman Reigns to reclaim his throne as WWE's most important star.

The OTC's own journey should be an inspiration for Rhodes. Reigns finally turned heel in 2020 after years of struggling to sell the audiences on his top man status.

His heel run instantly added layers to Reigns' character that continues to showcase since turning back face, and the fans have universally accepted The OTC.

Let The American Nightmare become the biggest problem on SmackDown, throwing his weight around into the new year to get what he wants.

He can be the crowd-hating villain that Cena wanted to be, and the crowd will accept it far more readily.

He can lean into the hammier side of his acting that has allowed him to start breaking out in Hollywood. He could even ask for some help from The Rock, emulating his "Hollywood" character.

As long as Rhodes is having fun with it as he was back in the day when he was "Undashing", The American Nightmare will win back over the audience to set up a natural face turn by WrestleMania 44.

In the meantime, Rhodes would instantly become SmackDown's top heel and give the brand a real top threat to win any title.

articles.title: 7 Trade Landing Spots for Auston Matthews Amid NHL Rumors

articles.body:
The NHL's March 1 trade deadline is still more than three months away. But the Toronto Maple Leafs, one of the league's biggest draws, had stumbled to a .391 points percentage entering Thursday's games, leaving them 27th overall—far closer to the basement than the penthouse.

So it's not surprising that Auston Matthews, at least according to league insider Pierre LeBrun, would be considered a prime player to move if GM John Chayka decides to steer head-on into a rebuild rather than a reload.

The 29-year-old center is in the third year of a four-year deal paying him $13.25 million annually , and given his status as a former Rookie of the Year, goal-scoring champion, and Most Valuable Player, he is expected to approach the $20 million threshold if he reaches unrestricted free agency in the summer of 2028.

Will Toronto soon experience "life after Matthews?"

And if so, where might he go to create the void? The B/R hockey team got together to discuss the point and came up with seven possible destinations for the California-born captain, who struck gold with Team USA at the 2026 Olympics.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

There's not a team on the list that needs a Matthews-type infusion any more than the Blackhawks, for whom three seasons with former No. 1 overall pick Connor Bedard have yielded three eighth-place finishes in the Central Division and the prolonging of a playoff drought that stretches back to 2020.

A projection of more than $36 million in cap space next season doesn't hurt the prospect of Matthews in the Windy City either, eh?

On the flip side, there might not be a team on this list that'd be more attractive to Matthews than the Devils, who just added a franchise goalie in Connor Hellebuyck, are residing in the upper tier of the NHL standings, and have a pair of fellow Team USA stars in Hellebuyck and forward Jack Hughes.

Don't forget, too, that Chayka might just be happy to pick up high-end defensive center Nico Hischier, yet another former No. 1 pick (along with Hughes and Matthews), if he were to pull the trigger on a trade.

If Matthews is still feeling the Olympic vibe into slide No. 3, the Rangers can offer his Team USA coach, Mike Sullivan, and a teammate, J.T. Miller, alongside the chance to play regularly in the "World's Most Famous Arena," and maintain his affiliation with one of the league's Original Six franchises.

After all, if he can make it there (or in a pressure-cooker like Toronto, for that matter), he can make it anywhere.

Ranking the Players Likely to Request a Trade 📊

The Penguins can't offer the Olympic connections available in New Jersey and New York, but they've got history on their side if Matthews decides he's moved by the prospect of heading to a city with a chance to follow franchise cornerstones named Mario Lemieux and Sidney Crosby.

Pittsburgh projects for nearly $60 million in cap space next season, and an interesting wild card is the presence of former Toronto GM Kyle Dubas, who signed Matthews to a five-year, $58.2 million deal in 2019.

The Edmonton captain/center was considered a potential future Shark after successfully bonding with San Jose's Macklin Celebrini with Team Canada at the Olympics, but the Oilers' hot start has put the brakes on trade talk surrounding No. 97, leaving an opening for Matthews.

Not only does GM Mike Grier have nearly $30 million in cap space with which to pay Matthews, but he's also got first-round picks from 2027 to 2030 and no fewer than 13 rostered skaters under age 30 to use as possible collateral for a trade.

Where other teams have Olympic ties, tradition, and cash, the Mammoth have location, location, location.

Matthews was born in California but moved to Arizona with his family as an infant, which could make the prospect of playing for the franchise formerly known as the Coyotes an appealing one.

And lest anyone forget, Utah's prospect pipeline is highly regarded by people who judge such things, and a projection of better than $24 million in cap space next season doesn't exactly hurt the team's chances either.

It's a legit fever dream for every current Western Conference contender.

As if it weren't bad enough that the Golden Knights are in the mix for every big-name player whose name comes up in trade rumors, the reality of what a 1-2 punch with Matthews and Jack Eichel (yep, another Team USA colleague) could yield is competitively terrifying.

Teammates or not, the respect is already there.

"(Eichel) is a special player," Matthews told the National Post as a rookie. "His stride, his skating ability and his strength … he's so hard to knock off the puck. He has that deceptive stride—he takes one and he's already by you."

articles.title: Andy Murray reacts as Leon Smith steps down as Team GB Davis Cup captain
articles.summary: Leon Smith will step down from his role as Team GB Davis Cup captain after almost 17 years in charge, following the conclusion of the...
articles.body:
Leon Smith will step down from his role as Team GB Davis Cup captain after almost 17 years in charge, following the conclusion of the 2026 Davis Cup Finals in Bologna.

The British coach guided his nation to their first Davis Cup win in 79 years when Andy Murray and co. lifted the trophy in 2015. Even since Murray's retirement, Smith and Team GB have continued to punch above their weight, and will play for the title in Bologna next week.

After such a legendary stint in charge, it's no surprise that so many were quick to congratulate and thank Smith. One of the first to do so was Murray , who won 45 Davis Cup matches for his country.

Andy Murray says Leon Smith got 'the best out' of Team GB as he remembers 2015 Davis Cup win

"Winning the Davis Cup in 2015 with Leon [Smith] as captain was one of the proudest moments of my career. He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play," said Murray.

"He got the best out of us that year. I've obviously known Leon a long time, since he coached me as a kid. I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup, and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments. I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain."

2015 Davis Cup final (Great Britain vs Belgium)

Andy Murray/Jamie Murray (Great Britain)

Smith relied upon Murray throughout his tenure as Davis Cup captain, but never more so than in the 2015 Davis Cup final. With Great Britain trailing 1-0 against Belgium in Ghent, Murray won three matches in a row to secure a famous away victory.

A press release from the LTA confirmed that 'succession planning considerations have been under review for some time' and that 'it is anticipated that a new Davis Cup captain will be appointed in the coming weeks.' BBC Sport have reported that Murray isn't believed to be interested in the role.

Leon Smith can still have perfect send-off by winning the 2026 Davis Cup

Smith's time as Team GB captain is drawing to a close, but there is still work to be done. Great Britain are one of eight sides in contention for the Davis Cup title at the Finals event in Bologna.

The eight teams in the 2026 Davis Cup Finals

Smith will take Arthur Fery, Cameron Norrie, Henry Patten, and Neal Skupski into the Davis Cup Finals as one of the four unseeded nations. Great Britain will play the third seeds, Germany, likely to be led by world number one Alexander Zverev, in the quarter-finals.

Great Britain's Davis Cup team (2026 Finals)

If Smith can guide his team to an upset win, they will meet Austria or Carlos Alcaraz's Spain in the semi-finals. Then, in the final, Great Britain could play the three-time defending champions Italy, South Korea, Czech Republic, or Canada.

The 2026 Davis Cup Finals begin on Tuesday, November 24. Great Britain will play their quarter-final match against Germany two days later, on Thursday, November 26.

articles.title: Houston leaves no doubt who should be college basketball’s new No. 1
articles.summary: The Cougars bullied Florida, blitzed Kansas and left Las Vegas with a title and the best résumé in the country.
articles.body:
Kelvin Sampson and his Houston Cougars are back.

Men's college basketball is about to have a new No. 1 team, and there's no doubt Houston belongs at the top after beating No. 9 Kansas 92-83 to win the Players Era 8 tournament, capping one of the most impressive runs of the young season.

As the premier early season event , there's plenty of value in navigating the loaded field in Las Vegas and emerging victorious. Just ask Michigan last season.

Houston didn't just win. The Cougars were dang near perfect.

After taking down No. 1 Florida in the semifinal , the Cougars faced a Big 12 foe in Kansas that could very well meet them again in the conference championship game, possibly even the Final Four.

Against the Jayhawks, though, it didn't look like a big-time battle. It looked like a coming-out party for Houston.

The Cougars came right out and did what they do best: make life extremely annoying for opponents with relentless defense. Then came what quite possibly separates this team from the rest of the country: the complementary offense.

Bill Self couldn't burn through his timeouts fast enough as Houston made life look way too easy around the basket, putting the Jayhawks in a blender for easy buckets Kansas couldn't seem to stop. It was a dominant first half. Houston led by as many as 24 points and entered halftime with 54, the most it has scored against a top-25 team in the past 30 years.

Even when Kansas staged a furious comeback behind freshman star Tyran Stokes, cutting the deficit to four points with just under three minutes remaining, Houston didn't flinch. The Cougars scored the next eight points to put the dagger in.

It took three tries, but Houston has finally emerged from Players Era as a champion after unsuccessful attempts in 2024 and 2025.

There will be massive reshuffling in the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll after the top four teams all lost , and you don't have to look far to see who should be the new No. 1 on Monday, Nov. 23: the Cougars themselves.

Not only did Houston win the Players Era 8, but it also had the toughest path of any team in the field as the only one to play two top-10 opponents.

The Cougars bullied the Gators in the rematch of the 2025 national championship game , unfazed by the pristine frontcourt of Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon and Rueben Chinyelu. Houston outmuscled Florida inside while guard Dedan Thomas Jr. lit up the Gators.

If anything, the Cougars' toughest challenge came against Rutgers in the opening round, a game they still won by 12 points.

Of the other top-10 teams still perfect, including Virginia, Texas and UCLA, none can compare to Houston's early résumé. The Cougars took down No. 1 and then one of the hottest offenses in the country, with both opponents ranked in the top four of KenPom . No one has wins as good as those.

Being No. 1 doesn't mean that much in mid-November. Sampson will be the first one to tell you that. But his team has proven it should jump all the way from No. 7 to the top spot for the first time since March 2024 while remaining a title contender that could very well earn a No. 1 seed in March for the fourth time in five seasons.

While Houston hasn't had much success at Players Era, it has been able to use those disappointments to spark strong regular seasons.

Now, after finally winning it, the Cougars hope an early season title can translate into the all-important, and still elusive, one in the NCAA Tournament.

articles.title: C.J. Jones - an Ohio State, Alabama recruiting target - leads Westlake to UIL playoff win
articles.summary: C.J. Jones ran for 132 yards and five touchdowns in the first half as Westlake routed San Antonio Pieper 59-14 in a Class 6A DII area-round playoff game.
articles.body:
SAN MARCOS - C.J. Jones swears he doesn't have anything to do with it.

Westlake's freshman phenom, who has college scholarship offers from just about any school you can think of, said the 132 yards and five touchdowns he ran for in the first half Thursday were a result of everyone else .

"I don't really take any of the credit," said Jones, who is now 28 yards shy of 1,000 rushing for the season. "I have to give it all to the offensive line. They made the holes. I just ran the play like what the coach said, hit the hole and scored."

It's an admirable trait for Jones to be modest with the spotlight that will be on him during his high school career. And while he did make several defenders miss once he got past the line of scrimmage, he is correct in that Westlake's offensive line was dominant during a 59-14 win over San Antonio Pieper in a Class 6A Division II area-round playoff game at Rattler Stadium.

The Chaps (11-1) ended with 279 yards rushing, a number that would have been far higher had they not maintained good field position thanks to their defense and special teams.

"It's insane running behind those guys," Jones said. "They make the gaps and just make me feel safe out there."

Jones scored on runs of 23, 11, 11, 34 and 3 yards as Westlake built a 38-0 halftime lead. He spent the entire second half on the sideline and probably could play as soon as Saturday if he needed to with as few hits as he took.

Westlake's rushing attack didn't slow down without Jones, though. Chase Brodhead, Isaiah Mills and Pete Fredenburg all scored rushing TDs as the Chaps at one point led by 52.

"We kind of knew going in we could run the ball," Westlake coach Tony Salazar said. "They had some man-to-man coverage out there, and it's scary to take a shot on first down and then turn around and look at second-and-10 in the face, so in order to stay ahead of the chains, running the ball was essential."

Jones should have at least two more games - Westlake will be a heavy favorite in the regional semifinals - to surpass 1,000 yards for the season and add to his 21 touchdowns. But whether he'll take credit for any of it is another question.

"Of course it feels amazing to score five touchdowns in a playoff game, but it's the front five and the coaches," he said.

Westlake's defense clamps down on dangerous Pieper offense

Pieper (7-5) entered the contest averaging more than 486 yards of offense and features four-star wideout Carson Lacombe , who has offers from 19 Power Four schools.

But Westlake (11-1) held the Warriors to 68 yards in the first half and Lacombe finished with five catches for 7 yards.

"Our pass rush was getting there quick," said Chaps defensive lineman Colton Fromberg, who was part of a front four that produced four sacks. "The quarterback had to get the ball out quick, and our secondary stepped up."

The Warriors abandoned their rushing attack in the first half, something Salazar called "surprising." They only ran the ball twice, and Westlake's linebackers and secondary adjusted to a pass-happy attack.

"There were a bunch of crossing routes and our kids were all over it," Salazar said. "And when they did complete a pass, there wasn't much space. … Our guys did a good job matching routes."

Westlake will play the winner of San Antonio Sotomayor vs. Edinburg Vela in the regional semifinals. In addition to an extra day of rest, it will carry momentum from two straight playoff wins by 45 points.

"We knew they were a good team, and we just completely dominated from the start," Fromberg said. "It's a huge morale boost."

articles.title: Lineup leaks in fantasy soccer game give Premier League clubs cause for consternation
articles.summary: As one of the most meticulous coaches in soccer, Mikel Arteta likes to have every base covered in his quest to win titles with Arsenal.Turns out his players...
articles.body:
As one of the most meticulous coaches in soccer, Mikel Arteta likes to have every base covered in his quest to win titles with Arsenal.

Turns out his players giving away squad secrets through an online fantasy game is an area he hasn't been able to control.

In the latest example of a growing issue for Premier League managers, Arsenal winger Christos Tzolis unwittingly gave away a clue that he would be returning to action after a month-long injury absence by selecting himself in his own team in the Fantasy Premier League game played by more than 11 million people worldwide.

That information was picked up by some of the fantasy game's eagle-eyed content creators and, sure enough, Tzolis was named in Arsenal's team the very next day for the English champions' 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.

Guarding team selections is a big deal in soccer — hence limits to the presence of media at practice sessions and the furor that erupted when Southampton was found to have used an analyst to carry out the unauthorized filming of opponents in training last season.

And so, Arteta has taken measures to combat the problem, with The Athletic reporting that he has banned Arsenal's players from including themselves or their teammates in their fantasy lineups.

On Friday, Arteta spoke about the issue, saying it has had an impact "with Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well."

"Constantly they are asking me about the lineups as well because they want to know," he said with a laugh, before adopting a more serious tone.

"It is a topic, a thing that is happening in our society right now and it's something new — we've haven't (previously) dealt with it. We need to put new things in place."

Arteta insisted that "confidentiality is something critical" for teams wanting to be successful.

"Because it's about trust, about what you are trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret," he said. "And we'll take measures to make sure it doesn't happen again."

Earlier this month, the BBC reported that an email was sent by Chelsea to its staff, warning them about the possible consequences of making team selections in Fantasy Premier League using their inside information about injuries.

That came after Chelsea striker Joao Pedro was removed from the fantasy teams of teammate Morgan Rogers and other staff members before news of an injury to the Brazilian had been made public.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso later said he was "not into the fantasy team thing," so was unaware.

articles.title: ACC Roundup: A Perfect Wednesday
articles.summary: Is Notre Dame legit?
articles.body:
There were five ACC teams in action on Wednesday night, and all won: Louisville beat Stetson, 83-69, Notre Dame clawed Auburn 78-73, NC State raced past Murray State, 93-83, Stanford stung Sacramento State, 78-65, and Cal sent East Texas A&M home miserable, 86-54.

Stetson started off hot, hitting 9 of their first 12 shots before Louisville woke up. Down 22-14, Flory Bidunga scored 7 straight points to rally the home team.

Stetson held the lead until about the 5:31 mark, which is impressive.

In the second half, Louisville cranked up the D, forcing Stetson to miss 18 of 20 attempts over about nine minutes.

Incidentally, Karter Knox took Seth Trimble's starting spot and finished with 14 points and 10 rebounds.

Is it just us, or is it nice to see a bit of optimism for Notre Dame? The Irish are now 6-1, with the one loss to Florida.

Against Auburn, the Irish started hot, going up 42-36 at the half, and shooting 50 percent.

Auburn battled back in the second, but the Tigers missed six straight free throws late in the second half, then Braeden Smith hit a tough shot in the lane to put Notre Dame up by 77-73. Brady Koehler, who is getting some NBA buzz, stole Auburn's inbounds pass, and hit a free throw to put the game out of reach.

NC State was hot against Murray State, hitting 16-0f-28 threes for 57.1 percent. The defense was really good, too, holding the Racers to 2-12 in the first half, and limiting offensive threat Brayden Shorter to 2 points.

The defense let up in the second half, as Murray State scored 57, but State controlled this game. Paul McNeil scored 33, and Preston Edmead had 20.

On the downside, State coughed up 16 turnovers and lost the boards, 38-29.

Sacramento State outplayed Stanford in the first half, 36-34, before the Cardinal figured it out in the second half.

Stanford outscored Sacramento State 44-29 after the break, shooting 57.1 percent. A 10-0 run broke it open for the Cardinal.

Julius Price had 22 points to pace Stanford. Christian Bliss had 16, while Nick Townsend kicked in 11.

Cal broke the game open early, and never really was challenged. The Bears forced an impressive 24 turnovers, which they converted into 28 points.

Nojus Indrusaitis had 23 points, while Michael Cooper added 18.

articles.title: Pre-Feast week SoCon power rankings
articles.summary: Now a full two weeks into the college basketball season, I’ve had a chance to see everyone in the SoCon play so far, and this is my first edition of my power...
articles.body:
Now a full two weeks into the college basketball season, I've had a chance to see everyone in the SoCon play so far, and this is my first edition of my power rankings for the 2026-27 season. I have teams lower in this first release than I think they will finish, which is primarily based on the fact that I have either only seen them once, or I rewarded teams for getting a Division-I win or wins rather than loading up on non-Division I wins so far, so don't crucify me yet.

It's been an exciting first couple of weeks, and Tennessee Tech might be the favorite team I have watched so far based on style of play. I thoroughly enjoyed being able to watch the Golden Eagles take down a good Western Kentucky team last Sunday. I am extremely impressed with CBO Newton and the Golden Eagles' ability to shoot the three. The question will be for them is how they can defend.

I hope y'all enjoy the pre-Feast Week SoCon power rankings. Our next release will be after Feast Week. I hope everyone has a Happy and Blessed Thanksgiving.

The Paladins have looked good in their first three games, mediocre in the road win at Holy Cross, while struggling to find any kind of offensive rhythm in the loss at Belmont last time out. The Paladins have seen Collin O'Neal join already injured Cole Bowser and Mason Smith on the list of early-season injuries, though Smith and Bowser are expected to return from their respective injuries sooner rather than later. Tom House was able to garner the first SoCon Player of the Week honor early on in the season, highlighted by a 30-point outburst vs. Northern Iowa. House leads the Paladins at 17.8 PPG, while fellow fifth-year senior Charles Johnston adds 12.2 PPG and 7.6 RPG. It was Johnston's unfortunate technical foul just a little over five minutes into the second half that led to a Belmont 14-1 scoring run, completely changing the trajectory of the game, as Furman went without a field goal for nearly an eight-minute span and saw a 44-39 lead turn into a 53-46 deficit. Furman's Cameron Elwer is starting to heat up, as he scored 13 points to lead the Paladins in the road loss at Belmont Saturday night. He has dished out 17 assists without committing a turnover in 92 minutes of basketball as a rookie backup point guard this season. Furman won 78-71 at Radford Wednesday night.

Chattanooga, like ETSU, started its season with a pair of respectable performances at a pair of power-conference programs, taking on both then-No. 11 Louisville (L, 84-70) and also Dan Earl's alma mater, Penn State (L, 97-93). The second-most recent outing for Chattanooga saw it post one of the most impressive road wins to date in the non-conference, with a 77-70 win at former SoCon member Elon. In the Mocs 77-70 road win, they became just the fourth team in the past 21 outings against non-conference competition on Elon's home floor to emerge victorious. All four teams over that duration all hail from the SoCon, as Chattanooga joined Mercer and Furman, who accomplished the feat last season, and UNCG who did so in 2022. The key to winning the game for Earl's team was a 42-10 dominance in points in the paint, which matched its 42 points in the paint in the loss at Penn State. The Mocs moved to 21-3 when scoring 40 or more points in the paint against an opponent under Earl's leadership. Like Furman and ETSU, Chattanooga has also showcased depth, with four of its five starters averaging in double figures, led by Aussie point guard Kobe McDowell-White, who is averaging 13.8 PPG and 5.7 APG. The Mocs defeated Winthrop 90-79 as part of the SoCon-Big South Challenge to move over .500 for the first time.

East Tennessee State has been competitive in its two power-conference matchups this season and looked especially good in the second half against Campbell last time out, putting it together their best half of the season for a 68-53 win. To me, the Bucs and Paladins look like the frontrunners early on, and there is a big reason why. Both teams have tremendous depth. The notable improvement for ETSU has been point guard play that BJ Ward has provided early on this season. He scored a career-high 25 points in ETSU's season-opening, 75-65, loss to Arizona State in the first meeting between the two in more than 70 years. The Bucs controlled things early against North Carolina State before the Wolfpack hit a surge over the last eight minutes of the contest to drop a 77-63 contest at the Lenovo Center in Raleigh. The most encouraging sign for this Bucs team is that they are once again really good defensively, and that has been evident in all four games, and even against high-major opposition. The Bucs also showed the ability to hit the glass, especially in the last contest against the Camels, out-rebounding Campbell, 47-26. Marqus Marion totaled a career-high 12 points against the Wolfpack and a career-high 10 boards against Campbell. His role could be reminiscent of former Bucs player and current Mercer Bears key cog Karon Boyd.

For a first-year program that has yet to face a program in the league as of yet, the Golden Eagles have shown that they are more than worthy of being competitive in their first season as a SoCon member. After all, the Golden Eagles were able to score the biggest non-conference win so far, which was a 97-94 win over preseason Conference USA favorite Western Kentucky. On that night, 19 3-pointers would splash the bottom of the net, with Cbo Newton's 6-for-7 effort from long range highlighting a night that saw Tech shoot a ridiculous 52.8% (19-of-36) from 3-point land. Though there have been some lopsided defeats to power foes like Indiana (L, 90-66) and Mississippi State (L, 106-88), the Golden Eagles were competitive for large portions of those two contests. The ability to move even higher in the power rankings for Tobin Anderson's club will be solely based on their ability to defend for 40 minutes. This team reminds me a lot of 2021-22 Samford squad that Bucky McMillan nearly led all the way to a SoCon Tournament title game in just his second season as the head coach in Homewood. The Golden Eagles nearly put up 100 in a second straight game in a 98-77 win at UNC Asheville on Wednesday night.

I put Mercer at five on this list simply because this team has gone out and challenged itself early in the season, and it has at least one really good road win. The Bears have started the 2026-27 season with games against Virginia Tech (L, 96-67), Davidson (L, 88-76), West Virginia (L, 75-61), and Georgia Southern (W, 97-91 OT) with each of those games having been on the road. Mercer's signature win early was a 97-91 overtime win over a solid Sun Belt foe, in Georgia Southern. It was a game in which Ryan Ridder's club showed real grit to get back into the game and ultimately pull out the win over its former Trans America Athletic Conference rival. Five found their way into double figure in the gutsy win for the Bears, including the reigning SoCon Player of the Week Shane Cherry, who would finish the contest with 16 points, dished out eight assists and recorded five rebounds. The scrappy Bears were led in the win by one of the few returning players for Ridder, in Quinton Perkins II, who finished with 23 points. Karon Boyd as many expected is an X-factor for this team and will prove to be a major addition late in the fall as this season moves along. The Bears returned to action on Wednesday night traveling to take on a good Big South foe, in Presbyterian but fell 88-84.

The Terriers gave us a show in a 97-92 loss against a very good Queens team this past Saturday. There is plenty of reason to believe Wofford will be right in the thick of the SoCon title race this season, and much of what makes Kevin Giltner's team such a good basketball team could be seen in Saturday's loss in Charlotte. The Terriers have some unique pieces, like big man Cutter Sisk, who is going to be a force in the Southern Conference this season. Sisk is currently one of four Terrier players averaging in double figures, as he is posting 11.6 PPG and 3.4 RPG, while shooting 51.3% (20-of-39) from the field and is also connecting on 37.5% (3-of-8) from 3-point range. He's going to be an exciting player to watch as the season progresses. Another key for the Terriers will be the continued emergence of Cam Lowe, as the season progresses. The 6-foot-6 guard is a tough guard for any team in the SoCon, with a good mix of shooting ability and athleticism. He's off to a strong start for the Terriers, averaging 11.0 PPG and 4.2 RPG. Wofford's first two victories this season have come against non-Division I foes, in both Voorhees (91-47) and Allen (100-67), while losing to both power programs North Carolina (W, 109-79) and No. 8 Tennessee (L, 90-59) along with this past weekend's setback to a very good Queens team. The Terriers earned their first win over a DI team Wednesday night, as they defeated Charleston Southern 79-77.

Western Carolina has gone out and gone toe-to-toe with ACC blue blood North Carolina in a game, which according to head coach Tim Craft, the Catamounts did not play their best basketball. Had they done that, we might have been discussing on the of the greatest upsets in the modern history of the Catamounts basketball program, but rather it turned out to be an 80-72 setback. After a controversial flagrant foul turned that game late, the Tar Heels seized upon that momentum to win in the final six minutes of the contest. One of the real standout players in the lead for me so far has been Jaxon Prunty. He's an elite shooter and scorer for the Catamount, along with showing just how good of an athlete he is in the open floor, and his dunk in the open floor against Lipscomb in the early season is easily one of the dunks I've seen in the league in the early part of the season. The Catamounts picked up a gutty, 83-75, win on the road at UNC Asheville but fell in their most recent contest against a good Lipscomb team, 75-68 at the Ramsey Center this past Saturday night. This team is young and still learning, but it has the pieces to be a real factor in the league once again in 2026-27.

Samford will obviously be a team that finishes higher than where they are right now, but this is a team that hasn't had much of a chance to show us what they are about during the 2026-27 season, with only four games on the young season under their collective belts. Samford's second-most recent outing came against a very good Wright State that made the NCAA Tournament last season, and they handed the Bulldogs a 90-66 loss at the Pete Hanna Center over the weekend. Cooper Noard has been as good as advertised so far for the Bulldogs, as he is averaging 11.7 PPG and 3.3 RPG. Will Shaver is off to a strong start to the season, as the 6-foot-10, 265-pound big man is leading the team in scoring through the first three games of the season, as he is averaging 15.3 PPG and 6.7 RPG. This could be a breakout season for Shaver, who first transferred into Samford a couple of years ago. I also think the same can be said for Cade Norris, who transferred into Samford from Illinois State prior to last season. The Bulldogs topped USC Upstate 74-64 Wednesday tonight as a part of the SoCon-Big South Challenge. I don't expect Samford to remain this low, as Lennie Acuff is too good of a coach, and I expect the Bulldogs to be one of the select three or four teams to be competing for a SoCon title this season.

The Citadel has show us enough early this season to make me believe that last year was not a fluke, and that Ed Conroy has finally gotten the hang of this portal thingy. He's got talent and maybe the most since his return to Charleston. But his most talented player didn't come from the portal at all, in 6-foot-6 freshman wing forward Aaron Ekwere. He's athletic, and he has the kind of tools that will cause big time problems in the SoCon this season. He's arguably the top freshman in the Southern Conference, but they don't give out the "Freshman of the Year" award anymore in the SoCon. In his most recent outing against Clemson, he delivered his most impressive outing to date. Though the Bulldogs lost the game, 87-51, Ekwere kept the Bulldogs in the game in the first half, as his activity was bothersome to the Tigers. He finished the night with a double-double, posting 13 points and 10 rebounds. The Bulldogs also have one of the more interesting pieces, in 6-foot-7 Tyler Mrus, who is one of the best 3-point marksman in the league. He's been as outstanding shooting the basketball so far this season, connecting on 44.4% (16-of-36) from 3-point range this season, with all but seven of his field goals coming from beyond the arc this season. The Bulldogs will be back in action on Friday night, hosting nearby rival South Carolina State in a tip-off time slated for 7 p.m. EST at McAlister Field House.

VMI is a team that might have the most dangerous scoring tandem in the SoCon with Rickey Bradley Jr. and TJ Johnson leading the way for head coach Andrew Wilson's Keydets. Bradley Jr., who is the preseason SoCon Player of the Year as selected by the league's head coaches, and is one of four Keydets players averaging in double figures at 11.6 PPG and 5.2 RPG. Johnson is averaging 15.8 PPG to lead the team but finished only eight points in the most recent win, which was a 71-53 win over Mary Baldwin, ending a streak of 11-straight games in double figures for Johnson, which dates back to last season. This might be Wilson's best defensive team since he took over as the head coach prior to the 2022-23 season. That amoeba zone is going to be tough for anyone to deal with this season, and the Keydets enjoyed their most impressive performance in a 65-51 win over North Carolina Central just last week. VMI would rebound by getting a 65-51 win over North Carolina Central at Cameron Hall to improve to 2-2 in the mid-week win. Leading the way for VMI was once again Johnson, who finished with 18 points and posted a game-high four 3-pointers in the win for the Keydets, as he would be one of five VMI players to finish the contest in double figures. One of the things that has stood out significantly through the early portions of the season for the Keydets has been their play on the defensive end, as the Keydets were able to limit the Eagles to just 37.9% shooting from the field and just 6.7% (1-of-15) from 3-point range in the home win Johnson's brother, Trap Johnson, contributed 12 points, while Alexander Daushvili added 11. Bradley Jr. and Paulius Narvilas rounded out the Keydets in double figures in the contest, as each added 10 points apiece. VMI returned to the floor on Wednesday evening as a part of the SoCon-Big South challenge and fell at Longwood 82-76.

We didn't know what to expect from UNC Greensboro coming into the season, and as expected, it's been a mixed bag for the Spartans. The Spartans have looked good at times and looked like very much a work in progress at others in what is Jerod Haase's first season as head coach of a program that has been among the most successful in the SoCon over the past 11 seasons. Dionte Neal is the real deal. In fact, I might coin the phrase "The Real Deal Neal" for him for the remainder of the season, as he had a 26-point effort in UNCG's win over Lees-McRae. The Spartans struggled to create a substantial cushion before holding on for a 91-84 win at Bodford Arena. The Spartans dropped their first two Division-I games, with a 74-65 setback at Elon and an 82-72 setback at Missouri Valley Conference foe UIC. UNCG picked up its first Division-I win 78-72 over Gardner-Webb Wednesday.

articles.title: Geno Auriemma’s out-of-touch NIL comments hurting UConn women’s basketball
articles.summary: UConn women's basketball coach Geno Auriemma has an out-of-touch view on the NIL era, which could be hurting the program's recruiting.
articles.body:
It has been a slow start to the 2026-27 college basketball season for Geno Auriemma and the UConn women's basketball team. While the Huskies ranked No. 7 in the latest AP Top 25 poll, they are just 3-2 despite having one of the country's best players, Sarah Strong .

One of the growing concerns for the Huskies is the lack of success on the recruiting trail, after having recent success with players like Strong, Paige Buckers and Azzi Fudd . Unfortunately, during the early signing period, Auriemma landed just one top-10 recruit, No. 9-ranked Sydney Savoury.

This week, Kaleena Smith, the consensus No. 1 player in the Class of 2027, dropped her top three schools , which dropped the Huskies from her list of finalists. That highlighted Auriemma's struggles in the NIL era, with Smith whittling down her list to USC, UCLA, and Arizona State.

On Thursday night, Auriemma sounded off on the NIL era, and his out-of-touch, dismissive comments about not seeing the "value of paying a high school kid" showed exactly why UConn is struggling on the recruiting trail.

Geno Auriemma's Falling Behind In NIL Era

"I just don't see the value of paying a high school kid a million dollars to come out of high school that hasn't dribbled the ball one time in college," Auriemma said. "That's more than 90 percent of the best players in the world in the WNBA.

"We have an agent that talks to their agent because the kids and the parents lie to you. 'It's not about the money. It's about academics; about finding the right fit, and about the right experience.' No, it isn't. Just say it's about the money, and we can all live happily ever after."

It's understandable that Auriemma is frustrated with the current landscape of recruiting in the NIL era, but that could also be a sign that it's time to move on. Auriemma has had a legendary career and built one of the most prestigious programs in the country, but if he isn't going to adapt, then it's time to change course.

Alabama legend Nick Saban knew he wouldn't be able to keep up in the NIL era, so he called it quits. If the 72-year-old Auriemma is standing in the way of the Huskies rebuilding their roster with the best young players in the country, perhaps he should do the same.

Of course, if UConn can get back to winning and get past its early struggles, his out-of-touch comments can be put on the back burner, for now.

articles.title: Foxes announce new sponsor after porn actress row
articles.summary: Leicester City split with gambling firm BC Game after it named Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador.
articles.body:
Leicester City have announced a new main shirt sponsor after ending a partnership with a gambling firm following its appointment of a porn actress as its brand ambassador.

The League One side confirmed they have now partnered with Bossjob, an AI-powered recruitment and job-matching platform based in Singapore.

On Wednesday, the club announced its split with BC Game - which was named as a sponsor for the Foxes at the start of the 2024-25 season.

The club's commercial director, Russell Jones, said the new men's team sponsor would be in place for the remainder of the 2026-27 season.

The Foxes parted ways with BC Game, an online gambling company not available to UK users, after it named porn actress Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month.

Announcing the partnership , the firm posted a video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media, with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin."

In response, fan group The Foxes Trust said: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people.

"Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?"

On Wednesday, following the criticism, the club issued a statement, which said it and BC Game had "reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect".

In a further statement on Friday, the Foxes confirmed Bossjob will take up the front-of-shirt position from this Saturday at their League One match against Huddersfield Town.

Jones said: "We welcome Bossjob as our new principal partner for the remainder of the season and look forward to building a strong relationship over the coming months.

"Through the partnership, we look forward to introducing Bossjob to our supporters and wider audiences, while supporting the company's ambitions to develop its international profile."

The club said replica shirts featuring the new sponsor would be made available to fans "in the coming days".

Bossjob co-founder, Quak Kiat How, added: "We're pleased to begin this partnership with Leicester City, a football club with a proud history and a strong connection to its supporters and local community.

"We look forward to working with Leicester City throughout the remainder of the season."
