articles.title: Bubba Wallace’s Team Makes Another Risky Decision
articles.summary: 23XI Racing swapped crew chiefs for 2027, sparking fan outrage. Denny Hamlin defends the move while Wallace supporters demand answers.
articles.body:
23XI Racing is changing the leadership atop two of its teams for 2027, and Bubba Wallace will have a new voice directing his efforts from the pit box.

The organization announced Nov. 18 that Davin Restivo will replace Charles Denike as crew chief of Wallace's No. 23 Toyota. Denike will move to the No. 67 team to work with Corey Heim, who is preparing for his first full-time NASCAR Cup Series season. Tyler Reddick will retain Billy Scott as crew chief of the No. 45 team.

The changes follow a productive season for 23XI. The organization recorded eight victories in 2026, including six by Reddick and two by Heim. Wallace did not reach Victory Lane, but he finished the year with 17 top-10 results, five top-five finishes and two runner-up performances. Wallace and Denike had previously enjoyed success together, including their victory in the 2025 Brickyard 400. Their partnership ends after two seasons, with 23XI choosing to take a different approach as it looks to build a championship contender.

The team says the moves are about matching personnel strengths to each driver's needs. Dave Rogers, 23XI's senior director of competition, explained that Denike's calm leadership style should benefit Heim as he makes the jump to a full-time Cup schedule. Rogers also pointed to Restivo's relentless attitude and attention to detail as qualities that make him a good fit for Wallace.

Denny Hamlin, 23XI's co-owner, emphasized that the organization wants to build on its winning season rather than settle for its current results. "While this was a banner year for us in the win column, it has always been our goal to build a championship-caliber organization," Hamlin said in the team's announcement.

For Wallace, the change brings another opportunity to turn consistent finishes into victories. Restivo spent the past two seasons leading Riley Herbst's team at 23XI, so he already knows the organization and its expectations.

The new pairing will have to prove itself on the track, but 23XI is making clear that its ambitions extend beyond simply adding to its win total. The goal is to put all three teams in a stronger position to compete for a Cup Series championship .

articles.title: Liverpool boss Taylor impressed with goalscoring form of forward Olsson
articles.summary: Liverpool head coach Gareth Taylor says that forward Beata Olsson’s recent goalscoring form has been impressive.The Swedish international has netted six goal...
articles.body:
Liverpool head coach Gareth Taylor says that forward Beata Olsson's recent goalscoring form has been impressive.

The Swedish international has netted six goals in the last four games. She has helped Liverpool win three of those matches.

Speaking to the media ahead of this weekend's Barclays Women's Super League fixture against Chelsea, Liverpool head coach Taylor said that Olsson's run of form has been impressive whilst highlighting areas where she can improve further.

"Beata will always tell you that there's way more to come from her," Taylor said. "She's definitely a very hungry player, great to work with. She is very honest in her appraisal of herself in games and in training. Like most strikers, she is desperate to score in every game and is super-frustrated when she doesn't. Of course, she contributes more than that for us as a player, but you know that Beata has these spells where she really catches fire.

"For her, it will always be about how many chances she gets in a game, how many times she makes the goalkeeper work. The more she does that, the more chance she has of scoring. She is a good finisher, there is no doubt about that, but I think getting her in the right positions, getting players to connect with her more is really important for us as a team.

"She's been good. Six goals in four games is really impressive."

Latest opponents Chelsea arrive on Merseyside top of the Barclays Women's Super League table, but Taylor believes that his side will go into the game with confidence.

He said "It's a good game. We've both had quick turnarounds with us playing Wednesday night and it's an early kick-off as well.

"Good for us to be at St Helens. We had success in this fixture last year by taking a draw, but both teams will look slightly different to what they did then.

"We feel pretty confident that we can attack this game like we would any other game. Our performances against the top teams have been good and positive this season. Looking forward to the challenge."

Liverpool have won their last three games, scoring 11 goals in the process. Taylor says that The Reds had been impressive even before those positive results.

He said "Small wins for us, of course; two wins in the cup and a good win away at Brighton.

"We are good in confidence. I've spoken to the players a lot; even though our results before that were a little bit tricky, I was impressed with our performances and knew that we weren't far away from what we have achieved in the last three games. We've managed to score 11 goals against decent opposition in those three games.

"We know the challenge tomorrow is really tough. They have a good level of players and they're a good team, so we need to be at our very best to have a chance of taking points from the game."

Liverpool's Barclays Women's Super League fixture against Chelsea takes place at BrewDog Stadium in St Helens at 12.45pm on Saturday afternoon.

articles.title: Weather shouldn't be issue in Cardinals' Week 11 game vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: The Cardinals are expected to play in chilly, but not frigid conditions in Week 11.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals face the Kansas City Chiefs this weekend on the road in Kansas City, Missouri. Now that we are nearing the end of November, weather, and more specifically the cold, could be a factor in games.

That won't be the case when the Cardinals and Chiefs play.

The game kicks off at 1 p.m. ET (12 p.m. in Kansas City). Weather conditions will be pretty ideal.

While rain is predicted for the early morning, it should be partly cloudy and in the mid 40s in terms of temperature by kickoff. The high is expected to be about 51 degrees.

That is colder than the Cardinals typically play, as they play inside most of the season, but it shouldn't impact much in terms of game play.

Things certainly could be worse this time of year.

articles.title: Max Verstappen: “I really thought that we would not win a race this year”
articles.summary: Max Verstappen admits he expected a winless 2026 after Red Bull's rough start, crediting the team for a late surge
articles.body:
Heading into the Las Vegas Grand Prix on a run of eight consecutive podiums, Max Verstappen looks every bit the force who dominated Formula 1 earlier this decade. Back in March, however, the four-time world champion was braced for his first winless campaign since 2015.

Speaking during Las Vegas media day, Verstappen reflected on the scale of Red Bull Racing 's mid-season recovery during Formula 1's sweeping 2026 chassis and engine overhaul - the team's first year running its in-house Red Bull Ford power unit.

"Did I personally expect it to be like this after the first few rounds? For sure not," Verstappen said. "I really thought that we would not win a race this year and now we are constantly fighting for a win or close to it."

Across the first three rounds in Australia, China, and Japan, Verstappen managed just 12 points - finishing sixth in Melbourne, retiring in Shanghai, and crossing eighth at Suzuka - while publicly describing the RB22 as "completely undriveable" in China due to acute cornering balance issues. He went four races without a podium and endured 15 grands prix without P1, absorbing four retirements across China, Monaco, Great Britain, and the Netherlands.

Asked whether Red Bull's 2026 recovery mirrored its adjustments from a year earlier, Verstappen shut down the comparison immediately.

"No, no, not related at all. Because we, this year, have very, very different problems to last year," he said. "So, it was a combination of putting more performance on the car, but at the same time also just fixing some of our problems, which automatically would give us more performance."

That step-by-step progress extended beyond aerodynamics. "Also, engine side, we understood a lot more what we wanted from the engine," Verstappen noted. "Still, there's always room for improvement; we know that. That's what we are constantly working on."

The payoff arrived in autumn. Verstappen broke his P1 drought on 4 October in Malaysia, swept the sprint and grand prix in Singapore a week later, and added a third victory in Mexico City on 1 November. Coupled with second place in São Paulo, the surge lifted him to second in the drivers' championship on 279 points - 111 behind newly crowned champion Kimi Antonelli, yet 17 clear of George Russell - while keeping Red Bull third in the constructors' fight.

"Hats off to the whole team; they've done a really good job," Verstappen said. "But now, we also look forward, and yeah, still look into some of the weaknesses that we have and things that we want to change for next year to hopefully make the car even better."

articles.title: Two Spurs stars return to training ahead of Ipswich clash
articles.summary: Savio and Lucas Bergvall were both back in Tottenham training ahead of their match against Ipswich this weekend.The pair have both been ruled out with injury...
articles.body:
Savio and Lucas Bergvall were both back in Tottenham training ahead of their match against Ipswich this weekend.

The pair have both been ruled out with injury since the 1-1 draw against Manchester United last month . Savio with a muscular injury, and Bergvall with a knee injury.

After Mathys Tel went off injured against Leeds after a strong tackle from Jayden Bogle, Savio's reintroduction into the Spurs setup will be a massive boost for Roberto De Zerbi.

The Italian hinted that the Brazilian could return after the international break before their draw against Leeds, saying, "Mudryk and Savio after the international break."

Mykhailo Mudryk, who has been sidelined since his debut against Nottingham Forest in September, and Tel were both not pictured in training.

Asked after the Leeds clash about Tel's injury, De Zerbi said, "Bad injury. Now we have to make the medical checks and in the next day we will know the problem."

articles.title: Surprise stoic Usman Nurmagomedov gets philosophical after violent gang attack
articles.summary: PFL lightweight champ Usman Nurmagomedov has broken his silence following a several-day stint in an Abu Dhabi jail for attacking former UFC bantamweight cham...
articles.body:
PFL lightweight champ Usman Nurmagomedov has broken his silence following a several-day stint in an Abu Dhabi jail for attacking former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili.

Nurmagomedov and several friends approached Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi leading up to a Real American Freestyle event in the country. Upset over how Dvalishvili had slapped teammate Akhmed Gadjimagomedov in Georgia earlier this year, the men attacked Merab and his friend Saba Lazishvili.

All eight men including two who just filmed the incident were arrested and sentenced to six months in prison plus an $80,000 fine. Things were looking grim for the PFL lightweight champion and his gang until Khabib Nurmagomedov interceded on their behalf, earning them a release from jail and drop in fine to $40,000.

Now Usman has made his first post on social media since the entire affair went down.

"The moment you are hurt by an insult or pleased by praise, you are still a slave – Marcus Aurelius," Nurmagomedov wrote next to a black and white picture of himself modelling a jacket at a clothing store.

The meaning of this quote in Usman's context is clear: he's not about to let anyone's opinion on what happened with Merab Dvalishvili and Saba Lazishvili enslave his thoughts.

Historians have questioned whether the quote was actually made by Aurelius, a Roman emperor and the father of Stoicism, but it captures one of his key teachings: events themselves don't cause distress, only your reaction to them. But Aurelius was also quite clear on virtue being the only true good, and personal character (defined around wisdom, courage, justice, and temperance) being what matters the most.

Which of those four virtues was Usman exhibiting when he and seven other men violently attacked Dvalishvili and Lazishvili?

articles.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams on potential for increase in opposing blitzes
articles.summary: Coming off a game in which he struggled against the blitz, Bears quarterback Caleb Williams discusses the plan to confront a potential increase.
articles.body:
The last time we saw Caleb Williams under center for the Chicago Bears , it wasn't pretty. After a promising start, pressure from an aggressive Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense began to make some headway that resulted in Williams tossing four interceptions prior to the bye.

It was a game that saw Williams blitzed 63.4 percent of the time, the highest rate he's seen since Week 2 against Minnesota. His 59.5 percent completion percentage was a season worst, as was his -0.31 EPA per dropback. Given those struggles, it's natural to assume that teams could be ready to dial up the blitz even more in the coming weeks. It sounds like that's something for which Williams is preferred:

"Like you said, it's a copycat league. So it's going to show up at some point here soon. Who knows, it could be this week, it could be next week, it could be the week after, it could be postseason, when we get there, whenever that is. It's going to show up at some point. Like I said, we've gone back and looked at it already. We'll fix it. For myself in that situation, if it does happen; I mean, there's times when people get through, and it's happened throughout my career. It's going to happen for the rest of my career. Just get the ball out of bounds or anything like that. Then on the other ones, just don't make bad decisions."

Photos from the Bears' ugly 27-24 win over Bucs in Week 9

In general, Williams has managed to be productive against the blitz this season. His 758 passing yards against the blitz rank 10th in the league, with a +0.02 EPA per dropback that indicates he's at least slightly above average in facing it. Where he runs into some issues, however, is in efficiency. Against the blitz, Williams is just 24th in completion percentage (58.6) and 23rd in completion percentage over expected (-3.9). His pressure rate, at 47.5 percent, is also fifth-highest among quarterbacks.

So there are some adjustments that will need to have been addressed over the bye, both on the part of the scheme to alleviate some of the pressure and on Williams to exercise proper decision-making when facing the blitz. In any case, it sounds like it's something that he's acutely aware of and, ideally, will showcase improvement against in the season's second half.

articles.title: Tonda Eckert signs Southampton contract extension after ‘Spygate’ scandal
articles.summary: Eckert emerged from the storm of the ‘Spygate’ scandal with a six-week suspended ban
articles.body:
Tonda Eckert has signed a contract extension at Southampton after surviving the storm of the 'Spygate' scandal.

Eckert found himself under immense scrutiny after Southampton were caught spying on their Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough last season.

An investigation found Saints had also spied on two other teams that seasons and the club were subsequently kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points at the start of the season season, admitting to three breaches of EFL regulations.

Eckert accepted responsibility as Southampton opted to stand by their manager despite the controversy, and he was later given a six-week suspended ban - keeping him on the touchline barring any further offences.

And despite the hindrance of a points deduction, Southampton have started the season in fine form under Eckert, with the club five points off top spot.

The German has now been rewarded with a contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2029.

Eckert said: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now.

"There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come."
